Frederic Block:
{{Short description|American judge (born 1934)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2017}} {{Infobox officeholder | name = Frederic Block | image = Frederic_Block.png | caption = Block in 2018 | office = [[Senior status|Senior Judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] | term_start = September 1, 2005 | term_end = | office1 = Judge of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] | term_start1 = September 29, 1994 | term_end1 = September 1, 2005 | appointer1 = [[List of federal judges appointed by Bill Clinton|Bill Clinton]] | predecessor1 = [[Eugene Nickerson]] | successor1 = [[Brian Cogan]] | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1934|6|6}} | birth_place = [[Brooklyn]], New York City, U.S. | education = [[Indiana University]] ([[Bachelor of Arts|AB]])
[[Cornell University]] ([[Bachelor of Laws|LLB]]) }} '''Frederic Block''' (born June 6, 1934) is a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]]. He was appointed to the federal bench in 1994, and took senior status in 2005. ==Background== Born in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]], on June 6, 1934, Block spent his first years there before his family moved to the [[Upper West Side]] of [[Manhattan]].{{cite news|url = https://www.westvillageoriginals.com/2016/01/01/frederic-block/|title = Frederic Block|last = Minichiello|first = Michael D.|work = West Village Originals|date = January 1, 2016|accessdate = February 4, 2026}} He an [[Bachelor of Arts|Artium Baccalaureus]] from [[Indiana University]] in 1956 and a [[Bachelor of Laws]] from [[Cornell Law School]] in 1959. After law school, he was a clerk to the [[New York Supreme Court]], appellate division, from 1959 to 1961. He was in private practice of law in [[Patchogue, New York|Patchogue]] from 1961 to 1962, then in [[Port Jefferson, New York|Port Jefferson]], [[Centereach, New York|Centereach]], and [[Smithtown, New York|Smithtown]], moving back and forth between these locations from 1962 to 1994. During this time, he became an adjunct professor at [[Touro Law School]], beginning in 1992. In private practice, Block handled both civil and criminal cases, and trial and appellate work—even arguing a case before the [[Supreme Court of the United States]].{{cite news |last1=Lat |first1=David |title=An Afternoon with Judge Frederic Block, Author of 'Disrobed' |url=http://abovethelaw.com/2013/03/an-afternoon-with-judge-frederic-block-author-of-disrobed/ |access-date=May 26, 2016 |agency=Above the Law |date=March 26, 2013}}{{citation |title=Questionnaire for judicial nominees |url=https://archive.org/stream/confirmationhear05unit#page/772/mode/2up/search/Frederic+block |work=Confirmation hearings on federal appointments: hearings before the Committee on the Judiciary, United States Senate, One Hundred Third Congress, first session on confirmations of appointees to the federal judiciary, Part 5 |publisher=US GPO |page=773 |year=1995}} ===Personal life=== Block married Estelle Kaufman in 1960. Previously a resident of [[Port Jefferson, New York]], on [[Long Island]], Block moved to Manhattan's [[West Village]] upon his confirmation as a judge. ==Federal judicial service== On July 22, 1994, Block was nominated by President [[Bill Clinton]] to a seat on the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] vacated by [[Eugene Nickerson]]. Block was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on September 28, 1994, and received his commission the next day. He assumed [[senior status]] on September 1, 2005, and was succeeded by Judge [[Brian Cogan]].{{cite web |url=https://www.fjc.gov/history/judges/block-frederic |title=Block, Frederic – Federal Judicial Center }} In 2005, Block complained that the disparity in security between the federal courthouse in Brooklyn, compared to the federal courthouse in Manhattan, was like being a denizen of [[Fallujah during the Iraq War|Fallujah]] rather than the [[Green Zone]].{{Cite journal |last=Wolff |first=Eric |title=Furor in the Court |url=http://nymag.com/nymetro/news/people/columns/intelligencer/11725/ |journal=[[New York (magazine)|New York]] |date=April 8, 2005 |issue=April 18, 2005 |access-date=May 21, 2015}} ===Notable cases=== On April 15, 2004, Judge Block sentenced [[Gambino crime family]] boss [[Peter Gotti]] to 9 years and 4 months in prison for [[money laundering]] and [[racketeering]] charges.{{cite news |last=Newman |first=Andy |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/04/16/nyregion/gambino-crime-boss-or-not-peter-gotti-gets-9-year-term.html |title=Gambino Crime Boss or Not, Peter Gotti Gets 9-Year Term |work=The New York Times |date=April 16, 2004 |access-date=January 20, 2011}} Gotti had a subsequent conviction in the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York]] for plotting to murder informant and former Gambino [[underboss]] [[Sammy Gravano]].{{cite news |title=Mafia boss Peter Gotti sentenced to 25 years |url=http://www.mg.co.za/article/2005-07-28-mafia-boss-peter-gotti-sentenced-to-25-years |access-date=January 20, 2011 |newspaper=Mail & Guardian |date=July 28, 2005 |agency=Agence France-Presse}} In 2008, Judge Block ruled that the United States government could not use ethnicity as a factor in deciding to detain two Egyptian-born men on a plane. {{cite court |litigants=Farag v. United States |vol=587 |reporter=F.Supp. 2d |opinion=436 |pinpoint=443 |court=E.D.N.Y |date=2008 |url=https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/1753142/farag-v-united-states/}} The Judge stated that it was the first case post-[[September 11 attacks]] to address whether ethnicity may be used to establish criminal propensity under the Fourth Amendment.{{cite news |last1=Robbins |first1=Liz |title=Judge Rules That Suspects Cannot Be Detained Because of Ethnicity |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/11/25/nyregion/25lawsuit.html |access-date=May 26, 2016 |work=The New York Times |date=November 24, 2008}} Judge Block has stated that this is the matter he is most proud of. On September 30, 2015, a portion of a "seemingly never-ending dispute" over the printing of the [[Menachem Mendel Schneerson|Rebbe's]] [[Likkutei Sichos|Sichos]] came to an end when Judge Block dismissed a major part of a lawsuit involving members of the Orthodox Jewish [[Chabad]] group. Judge Block dismissed claims of copyright infringement and unfair competition brought by Vaad L'Hafotzas Sichos and Zalman Chanin against [[Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch|Merkos]] and [[Agudas Chasidei Chabad]].{{cite news |title=Judge Dismisses Majority of Vaad's Claim Against Kehot |url=http://crownheights.info/communal-matters/501824/judge-dismisses-majority-of-vaads-claim-against-kehot/ |date=October 1, 2015}} On May 24, 2016, Judge Block ordered a [[Sentence (law)|sentence]] of one year of [[probation]] (rather than the [[United States Federal Sentencing Guidelines|guideline]] 33-41 month imprisonment) for a defendant who was convicted by a jury of importation and possession of cocaine with the intent to distribute. {{cite court |litigants=USA v. Nesbeth |court=E.D.N.Y. |date=2016 |url=https://img.nyed.uscourts.gov/files/opinions/15cr18order.pdf}} In a 44-page [[Judicial opinion|opinion]], Judge Block claimed the "collateral consequences" facing convicted felons are punishment enough. Judge Block's opinion and call for reform appears to be one of the most detailed examinations of [[collateral consequences of criminal conviction|collateral consequences]] and sentencing.{{cite news |last1=Weiser |first1=Benjamin |title=U.S. Judge's Striking Move in Felony Drug Case: Probation, Not Prison |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/26/nyregion/in-a-striking-move-brooklyn-judge-orders-probation-over-prison-in-felony-drug-case.html |access-date=May 26, 2016 |work=The New York Times |date=May 25, 2016}} ==Other work== ===Books=== ====Nonfiction==== On July 17, 2012, Judge Block released his first book named ''Disrobed: An Inside Look at the Life and Work of a Federal Trial Judge''.{{cite web |last=Pierson |first=Brendan |title='Disrobed' offers look at life on the bench |url=http://www.dailyreportonline.com/PubArticleDRO.jsp?id=1202564378177&Disrobed_offers_look_at_life_on_the_bench&slreturn=20120817121649 |publisher=Daily Report Online |date=July 26, 2012}} The book was written for a behind the bench look at some of the most controversial cases in the past 20 years.{{cite web |last=Block |first=Frederic |title=When Every Day Is Judgment Day |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2012-07-12/when-every-day-is-judgment-day.html |publisher=Bloomberg |date=July 12, 2012}} The book covers Judge Block's approach to sentencing such as the [[death penalty]], [[racketeering]], [[gun laws]], [[drug laws]], [[discrimination law]]s, [[race riots]], [[terrorism]], and restitution of looted property to victims of [[the Holocaust]].{{cite web |last=Tallmer |first=Jerry |title=Judge's book gives an insider's view of life on the bench |url=http://www.thevillager.com/?p=6539 |publisher=The Villager |date=July 19, 2012}} On May 29, 2019, Judge Block released ''Crimes and Punishments: Entering the Mind of a Sentencing Judge.''{{Cite web |title=Crimes and Punishments: Entering the Mind of a Sentencing Judge |url=https://www.americanbar.org/products/inv/book/371170166/ |access-date=2022-09-09 |website=www.americanbar.org |language=en}} The book discusses several criminal cases, Judge Block's personal experiences and personal thoughts as they related to his duties; and demonstrates to the reader the power and responsibilities of a federal judge. In 2024, Judge Block released another book: ''A Second Chance: A Federal Judge Decides Who Deserves It''.{{cite news|last=Lennon|first=John J.|date=September 16, 2024|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/books/2024/09/16/frederic-block-second-chance-review/|title=A judge argues for expanding a Trump law that can free prisoners early|work=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=October 21, 2026}} The book again gives examples of real cases, this time to illustrate Block's belief that state judges (in addition to federal judges, who already have this power based on a 2018 federal law, the [[First Step Act]]) should have the authority to reduce previously imposed stiff criminal sentences and to grant "compassionate release" to deserving prisoners in extraordinary and compelling circumstances. ====Fiction==== In 2017, Block published a novel entitled ''Race to Judgment''.{{cite news|url = https://abovethelaw.com/2017/10/race-to-judgment-an-interview-with-judge-frederic-block/|title = Race To Judgment: An Interview With Judge Frederic Block |date = October 11, 2017|accessdate = February 4, 2026|work = Above the Law|last = Lat|first = Davod|authorlink = David Lat}} ===Theatre=== Block co-wrote a musical called ''Professionally Speaking'' with [[Peter K. Winkler]] and Ernst Muller, which was produced [[off-Broadway]] in 1986.{{cite web|url = https://www.spectra.theater/explore/production/a4b7c4ab-8d9b-5a32-b474-2f095c3484c4|title = Professionally Speaking (1986)|work = [[Internet Off-Broadway Database]]|accessdate = February 4, 2026}} Block's inspiration to write a musical began when he represented a [[theatrical troupe]] in a lawsuit in 1981.{{cite news|url = https://www.nytimes.com/1986/05/18/nyregion/lawsuit-leads-to-a-musical.html|title = Lawsuit Leads to Musical|date = May 18, 1986|accessdate = February 4, 2026|newspaper = [[The Hennessey]] of the [[Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts]] from 1972 to 1973. ==Career== Martone was in private practice in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] from 1973 to 1985, during which time he was a staff attorney to the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts from 1974 to 1975. ==Judicial service== Martone was a judge on the [[Superior Court of Arizona]] from 1985 to 1992, and a justice of the [[Supreme Court of Arizona]] from 1992 to 2001. On September 10, 2001, Martone was nominated by President [[George W. Bush]] to a seat on the [[United States District Court for the District of Arizona]] vacated by [[Roger Gordon Strand]]. Martone was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on December 13, 2001, and received his commission on December 21, 2001. [[Syracuse University College of Law|Syracuse University]] ([[Bachelor of Laws|LLB]]) | footnotes = }} '''Frederick James Scullin Jr.''' (born November 5, 1939) is an American lawyer who serves as a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of New York]]. ==Education and career== Scullin was born in [[Syracuse, New York]]. He attended [[Niagara University]] where he received a [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1961, and he graduated from [[Syracuse University College of Law]] with a [[Bachelor of Laws]] in 1964. After graduating from law school, Scullin served in the [[United States Army]] as an [[Infantry]] Commander in [[Vietnam]]. Scullin practiced law as a private attorney and in various prosecutors' offices from 1967 to 1982. In 1982 he was appointed [[United States Attorney]] for the [[Northern District of New York]] by President [[Ronald Reagan]]. He served in the position for ten years until 1992.{{FJC Bio|nid=1387546|inline=yes}} ===Federal judicial service=== On September 12, 1991, Scullin was nominated to the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of New York]] by President [[George H. W. Bush]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on February 6, 1992, and received his commission on February 10, 1992. He served as Chief Judge of the District from 2000 until March 13, 2006, when he assumed [[senior status]]. Scullin was also appointed by Chief Justice [[William Rehnquist|Rehnquist]] to the [[United States Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court]] for a term of seven years running from 2004 until 2011. ===Notable case=== On July 26, 2014, Judge Scullin struck down the [[District of Columbia]]'s ban on carrying handguns outside of a person's home, saying that the ban violated the [[Second Amendment to the United States Constitution|Second Amendment]].{{cite news|last1=Reeve|first1=Richard|title=Federal judge rules D.C. handgun ban unconstitutional|url=http://www.wjla.com/articles/2014/07/federal-judge-rules-d-c-handgun-ban-unconstitutional-105478.html|access-date=28 July 2014|publisher=WJLA ABC 7|date=27 July 2014|archive-date=30 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140730192350/http://www.wjla.com/articles/2014/07/federal-judge-rules-d-c-handgun-ban-unconstitutional-105478.html|url-status=dead}} He wrote that "there is no longer any basis on which this court can conclude that the District of Columbia's total ban on the public carrying of ready-to-use handguns outside the home is constitutional under any level of scrutiny."{{cite web|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/federal-judge-rules-washington-dc-handgun-ban-is-unconstitutional/|title=Federal judge rules Washington, D.C., handgun ban is unconstitutional|date=27 July 2014|work=cbsnews.com|access-date=1 July 2015}} In response to the ruling, the D.C. Metropolitan Police determined that non-residents bearing firearms in the district are subject to the handgun laws of their home jurisdiction; in effect, this makes the District much more permissive of firearms.{{cite web|last1=Hess|first1=Hannah|title=In D.C., Response to Judge's Handgun Ruling Is Mixed and Muddled (Updated)|url=http://blogs.rollcall.com/hill-blotter/dc-handgun-ruling-response-is-mixed-and-muddled/?dcz=emailalert|website=www.rollcall.com|publisher=Roll Call|access-date=29 July 2014|archive-date=10 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810010632/http://blogs.rollcall.com/hill-blotter/dc-handgun-ruling-response-is-mixed-and-muddled/?dcz=emailalert|url-status=dead}} On July 29, 2014, in response to a partially unopposed motion filed by the District of Columbia, Judge Scullin issued a 90-day stay of his initial order. The stay expired on November 28, 2014. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Sources== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1387546}} *[https://web.archive.org/web/20071026024044/http://www.nynd.uscourts.gov/bios/fjs.htm Official biography] from the District Court {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=Seat established by 104 Stat. 5089}} {{s-ttl|title={{nowrap|Judge of the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of New York]]}}|years=1992–2006}} {{s-aft|after=[[Mae D'Agostino]]}} {{s-bef|before=[[Thomas James McAvoy]]}} {{s-ttl|title={{nowrap|Chief Judge of the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of New York]]}}|years=2000–2006}} {{s-aft|after=[[Norman A. '''Grant Murray Snow''' (born October 20, 1959) is an American lawyer and jurist who serves as a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Arizona]]. Snow was previously a state court judge on the [[Arizona Court of Appeals]] from 2002 to 2008.

==Early life and education==
Snow was born in [[Boulder City, Nevada]]. He received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[Brigham Young University]] in 1984. He received a [[Juris Doctor]] from the [[J. Reuben Clark Law School]] at Brigham Young University in 1987.

==Career==
Snow started his legal career as a [[law clerk]] for Judge [[Stephen H. Anderson]] of the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit]] from 1987 to 1988. He was in private practice in [[Phoenix, Arizona]], from 1988 to 2002. He was a judge on the [[Arizona Court of Appeals]] from 2002 to 2008.

===Federal judicial service===
Snow was nominated by President [[George W. Bush]] on December 11, 2007, to a seat vacated by [[Stephen M. McNamee]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on June 26, 2008. He received his commission on July 23, 2008. He served as chief judge from 2018 to 2024. He assumed [[senior status]] on October 21, 2024.<ref>{{FJC Bio|nid=1392746|inline=yes}}</ref>

===Notable cases===
On May 24, 2013, Snow ruled that the [[Maricopa County Sheriff's Office]] (MCSO), and Maricopa County Sheriff [[Joe Arpaio]] violated the [[Civil Rights Act of 1964]], and committed acts of racial profiling against Hispanics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://i2.cdn.turner.com/cnn/2013/images/05/25/arpaio.case.pdf |title=PDF of Judge Snow's ruling|date=May 24, 2013|access-date=May 25, 2013}}</ref>  The judge will also preside over the [[United States Department of Justice]]'s lawsuit to gain access to MCSO's documents and facilities, as part of the department's investigation of alleged discrimination in MCSO's police practices and jail operations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ktar.com/category/local-news-articles/20100920/Judge-picked-for-records-lawsuit-against-sheriff/ |title=Judge picked for records lawsuit against sheriff |date=September 20, 2010 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=Bonneville International. |access-date=September 30, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719095540/http://ktar.com/category/local-news-articles/20100920/Judge-picked-for-records-lawsuit-against-sheriff/ |archive-date=July 19, 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/2010/September/10-crt-993.html |title=Justice Department Files Lawsuit Against Maricopa County Sheriff's Office For Refusing Full Cooperation With Title VI Investigation |date=September 2, 2010 |work=The United States Department of Justice |access-date=September 30, 2010}}</ref> On January 15, 2015, he announced that he would be bringing civil contempt charges against the MCSO, with a hearing to be held in April,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/phoenix/2015/01/16/arpaio-federal-contempt-hearing-april-abrk/21869887/|title=Judge: Arpaio will face contempt hearing in April|author=Megan Cassidy|date=January 16, 2015|access-date=January 17, 2015}}</ref> and on August 19, 2016, as one result of those proceedings, he issued an order requesting that the United States Attorney for the Arizona district  prosecute Arpaio and three of his MCSO associates for criminal contempt.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2016/08/20/us/arpaio-criminal-contempt-charges-referral/index.html/|title=Judge seeks criminal contempt charges against Sheriff Joe Arpaio|author=Kimberly Hutcherson|website=[[CNN]] |date=August 20, 2016|access-date=August 20, 2016}}</ref>

'''Gail Allison Weilheimer''' ({{nee|'''Zuckerman'''}}; born 1970)<ref name="Questionnaire">{{Cite web|url=https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/weilheimer_sjq.pdf|title=Questionnaire for Judicial Nominees|publisher=United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|access-date=July 30, 2024}}</ref> is an American lawyer who has served as a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania]] since 2025. She previously served as a judge of the [[Pennsylvania courts of common pleas|Montgomery County Court of Common Pleas]] from 2014 to 2025.

== Education ==

Weilheimer received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in 1992 from [[Hofstra University]] and a [[Juris Doctor]] in 1995, from the [[Maurice A. Deane School of Law]] of Hofstra University.<ref name="WHBio">{{Cite press release |title=President Biden Names Fifty-Second Round of Judicial Nominees |date=July 3, 2024 |publisher=The White House |location=Washington, D.C. |url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/presidential-actions/2024/07/03/president-biden-names-fifty-second-round-of-judicial-nominees/ |access-date=July 3, 2024}} {{PD-notice}}</ref>

== Career ==

From 1995 to 2002, Weilheimer served as an assistant district attorney in the [[District Attorney of Philadelphia|Philadelphia District Attorney's Office]]. In 2002, she worked as an associate at Abrahams, Loewenstein and Bushman, P.C. in [[Philadelphia]]. From 2003 to 2006, she was a litigation associate, where she focused on [[criminal defense]] practice at Frank, Rosen, Snyder and Moss in [[Elkins Park, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="Pottsmerc">{{Cite web |last=Hessler, Jr. |first=Carl |date=November 5, 2013 |title=Two veteran lawyers elected to Montco bench |url=https://www.pottsmerc.com/2013/11/05/two-veteran-lawyers-elected-to-montco-bench/ |access-date=July 3, 2024 |website=The Mercury |language=en-US}}</ref> From 2006 to 2013, she worked as a senior counsel at Wisler Pearlstine, LLP in [[Blue Bell, Pennsylvania]],<ref name="WHBio" />  She was an [[Abington Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania|Abington Township]] commissioner from 2004 to 2008.<ref name="Pottsmerc" />

In November 2013, Weilheimer was elected as a judge of the [[Pennsylvania courts of common pleas|Montgomery County Court of Common Pleas]], running as a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] and receiving 63,084 votes, defeating her [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] opponent Sharon Giamporcaro, who received 58,906 votes.<ref name="Pottsmerc" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zatzariny Jr. |first=Tim |date=November 6, 2013 |title=Two Democrats Win Montco Judgeships |url=https://patch.com/pennsylvania/abington/two-democrats-win-montco-judgeships_63196552 |access-date=July 3, 2024 |website=Abington, PA Patch |language=en}}</ref> She served in that position from 2014 to 2025.<ref name="WHBio" />

=== Federal judicial service ===

On July 3, 2024, President [[Joe Biden]] announced his intent to nominate Weilheimer to serve as a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania]]. On July 8, 2024, her nomination was sent to the Senate. President Biden nominated Weilheimer to the seat vacated by Judge [[Gene E. K. Pratter]], who died on May 17, 2024.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Nominations Sent to the Senate |date=July 8, 2024 |publisher=The White House |location=Washington, D.C. |url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/presidential-actions/2024/07/08/nominations-sent-to-the-senate-151/}}</ref> On July 31, 2024, a hearing on her nomination was held before the [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|Senate Judiciary Committee]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nominations|date=July 30, 2024|publisher=United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|location=Washington, D.C.|url=https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/committee-activity/hearings/07/31/2024/nominations}}</ref>  During her confirmation hearing, Senator [[John Neely Kennedy]] questioned her about a case of a nursing home assistant who [[sexually assaulted]] an elderly, incapacitated woman with [[Alzheimer's disease]], whom Weilheimer sentenced to eleven months for the crime following a [[plea deal]].<ref>https://www.thereporteronline.com/2017/06/28/man-convicted-of-sexual-assault-pleads-guilty-to-dui-charge/</ref>{{relevance inline|date=September 2024}} On September 19, 2024, her nomination was reported out of committee by an 11–10 [[party-line vote]].<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Senate Judiciary Committee Advances Four Judicial Nominations, Two Marshal Nominations To Full Senate |date=September 19, 2024 |publisher=U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee |url=https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/press/dem/releases/senate-judiciary-committee-advances-four-judicial-nominations-two-marshal-nominations-to-full-senate |access-date=September 20, 2024}}</ref> On November 21, 2024, the [[United States Senate]] invoked [[cloture]] on her nomination by a 51–47 vote.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1182/vote_118_2_00302.htm|title=On the Cloture Motion (Motion to Invoke Cloture: Gail A. Weilheimer to be U.S. District Judge for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania)|website=United States Senate|date=November 21, 2024|access-date=November 21, 2024}}</ref> On December 3, 2024, her nomination was confirmed by a 50–48 vote.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1182/vote_118_2_00308.htm|title=On the Nomination (Confirmation: Gail A. Weilheimer, of Pennsylvania, to be U.S. District Judge for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania)|website=United States Senate|date=December 3, 2024|access-date=December 3, 2024}}</ref> She received her judicial commission on January 2, 2025,<ref>{{FJC Bio|nid=13761902|inline=yes}}</ref> and was sworn in on January 3, 2025.<ref>{{Cite press release|date=January 3, 2025|title=Press Release - Honorable Gail Weilheimer sworn in as United States District Judge|url=https://www.paed.uscourts.gov/sites/paed/files/documents/Press_Release_Weilheimer.pdf|website=paed.uscourts.gov|access-date=January 4, 2025}}</ref>

He received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[California State University, Los Angeles]], in 1972, a [[Master of Social Work]] from the [[George Warren Brown School of Social Work]] at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1976, and a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[California Western School of Law]] in [[San Diego]] in 1976. In 1972, he was the manager of a liquor store based in Los Angeles, California. From 1974 to 1976 he served as a law clerk for three different organizations and law firms before becoming a legal intern with the [[San Diego County District Attorney|San Diego District Attorney's Office]] in 1976. He was a deputy district attorney of [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]], California from 1976 to 1978, and then a deputy city attorney for that city from 1978 to 1979. He was a deputy chief of the Civil Division of the [[United States Attorney]]'s Office for the Eastern District of California from 1979 to 1985. He was a business litigator, Stockman Law Corporation from 1985 to 1986. He was a senior deputy attorney of Sacramento from 1986 to 1990, and then returned to the United States Attorney's Office as chief of the Civil Division until 1992.{{FJC Bio|nid=1378611|inline=yes}} ===Federal judicial service=== On August 1, 1991, Burrell was nominated by President [[George H. W. Bush]] to a new seat on the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of California]] created by 104 Stat. 5089. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on February 27, 1992, and received his commission on March 2, 1992. He served as chief judge of the district from 2007 to 2008. Burrell assumed [[senior status]] effective July 4, 2012. He was in private practice in [[Platte City, Missouri|Platte City]], [[Missouri]] in 1973. He was an assistant [[city attorney]] of City of St. Joseph from 1973 to 1977. He was a business law instructor, [[Webster College]] from 1976 to 1977. He was in private practice in St. Joseph, Missouri from 1977 to 1979. He was a Circuit judge on the Fifth Judicial Circuit Court of Missouri from 1979 to 1987. He was a judge on the [[Missouri Court of Appeals]], Western District from 1988 to 1996, serving as chief judge from 1994 to 1996. ==Federal judicial service== Fenner was nominated by President [[Bill Clinton]] on December 13, 1995, to be a United States District Judge of the United States District Court for the Western District of Missouri, to a seat vacated by [[Scott Olin Wright]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on July 10, 1996, and received his commission on July 25, 1996. He assumed [[senior status]] on September 8, 2015. === Undisclosed luxury travel === In May 2024, [[NPR]] revealed that Fenner had received free travel in December 2021 to the Breakers Colloquium, a privately funded legal seminar hosted at [[The Breakers (hotel)|The Breakers]] resort in [[Palm Beach, Florida|Palm Beach]], Florida, but had failed to disclose this on his required annual financial disclosure report for that year, in violation of federal law.{{Cite web |last=Dreisbach |first=Tom |last2=Johnson |first2=Carrie |date=2024-05-01 |title=When judges get free trips to luxury resorts, disclosure is spotty |url=https://www.npr.org/2024/05/01/1247512187/federal-judges-disclosures-luxury-trips |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501093641/https://www.npr.org/2024/05/01/1247512187/federal-judges-disclosures-luxury-trips |archive-date=2024-05-01 |access-date=2024-05-07 |website=[[NPR]]}} In response, Fenner told NPR, "I’m embarrassed about the fact that somehow that was overlooked by me. [[Yale University]] (MPPM, [[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''Gary Stephen Katzmann''' (born 1953) is an American lawyer who has served as a [[United States federal judge|United States judge]] of the [[United States Court of International Trade]] since 2016. He previously served as an associate justice of the [[Massachusetts Appeals Court]] from 2004 to 2016. ==Biography== Katzmann received an [[Bachelor of Arts|Artium Baccalaureus]] degree in 1973 from [[Columbia College, Columbia University|Columbia College]] at [[Columbia University]]. He received a [[Master of Letters]] in 1976 from the [[University of Oxford]]. He received a master's in public and private management in 1979 from the [[Yale School of Management|Yale School of Organization and Management]]. He received a [[Juris Doctor]] in 1979 from [[Yale Law School]]. He began his legal career by serving as a [[law clerk]] to Judge [[Leonard B. Sand]] of the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York]] from 1979 to 1980 and to Judge [[Stephen Breyer]] of the [[United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit]] from 1980 to 1981. From 1981 to 1983, he worked at [[Harvard Law School]]'s Center for Criminal Justice as a research associate and special investigator. From 1983 to 2004, he served in the [[United States Attorney]]'s Office for the District of Massachusetts, including as chief appellate attorney, deputy chief of the criminal division, and chief legal counsel to the United States attorney. While at the United States Attorney's Office, he was detailed to the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] from 1994 to 1995 and the Office of the Deputy Attorney General from 1993 to 1994. From 2004 to 2016, he served as an associate justice of the [[Massachusetts Appeals Court]] adjudicating civil and criminal matters.{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/07/30/president-obama-nominates-three-serve-united-states-court-international|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=President Obama Nominates Three to Serve on the United States Court of International Trade|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=July 30, 2015}}{{FJC Bio|nid=1394861|inline=yes}} His twin brother, [[Robert Katzmann]], served as chief judge on the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit]]. {{Cite episode| title=Q&A with Judge Robert Katzmann| url=https://www.c-span.org/video/?321130-1/qa-robert-katzmann&start=1288| access-date=12 Nov 2018| series=Q&A| series-link=Q&A (U.S. talk show)| network=C-SPAN| minutes=22:41| quote="That man is my identical twin brother, Gary."| transcript-url=https://www.c-span.org/video/transcript/?id=8826| transcript=(transcript)}} ==Trade Court service== On July 30, 2015, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Katzmann to serve as a United States Judge of the United States Court of International Trade, to the seat vacated by Judge [[Jane A. Restani]], who took [[senior status]] on March 1, 2015.{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/07/30/presidential-nominations-sent-senate|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=Presidential Nominations Sent to the Senate|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=July 30, 2015}} He received a hearing on his nomination on January 27, 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/meetings/nominations-01-27-16|title=United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|website=www.judiciary.senate.gov}} On April 7, 2016, his nomination was reported out of committee by [[voice vote]].{{cite web|url=https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/Results%20of%20Executive%20Business%20Meeting%20-%20April%207,%202016.pdf|title=Results of Executive Business Meeting – April 7, 2016, Senate Judiciary Committee|publisher=}} On June 6, 2016, the U.S. Senate confirmed Katzmann's nomination in a [[voice vote]]. He received his commission on September 15, 2016. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Sources== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1394861}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[Jane A. [[Yale Law School|Yale University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''Gary Richard Brown''' (born 1963) is a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] and former [[United States magistrate judge]] of the same court. ==Biography== Brown received his [[Bachelor of Arts]], ''[[cum laude]]'', from [[Columbia College (New York)|Columbia College]] in 1985 and his [[Juris Doctor]] from [[Yale Law School]] in 1988. Brown began his legal career as a [[law clerk]] to Judge [[Jacob Mishler]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] from 1988 to 1989. From 1989 to 1996, Brown served as an [[assistant United States attorney]] in the Civil Division, where he also served as affirmative litigation coordinator from 1994 to 1996. From 1996 to 2005, he served as an assistant United States attorney in the Long Island Criminal Division at the United States Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York, where he was elevated to deputy chief in 2001 and chief in 2003. From 2005 to 2011, Brown worked at [[CA Technologies]] as senior counsel, associate general counsel, and director for litigation, and then as chief compliance officer and chief counsel of litigation.[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/07/30/president-obama-nominates-seven-serve-united-states-district-courts "President Obama Nominates Seven to Serve on the United States District Courts" White House, July 30, 2015] == Federal judicial service == === United States magistrate judge === Brown served as [[United States magistrate judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] from 2011 to 2019. ===Expired nomination to district court under Obama=== On July 30, 2015, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Brown to serve as a United States District Judge of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]], to the seat vacated by Judge [[Sandra J. Feuerstein]], who assumed [[senior status]] on January 21, 2015.[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/07/30/presidential-nominations-sent-senate "Presidential Nominations Sent to the Senate" White House, July 30, 2015] He received a hearing before the [[United States Senate Judiciary Committee]] on October 21, 2015.[http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/meetings/nominations-10-21-15 "Nominations", United States Senate Judiciary Committee, October 21, 2015] On November 5, 2015, his nomination was reported out of committee by a [[voice vote]].[http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/Results%20of%20Executive%20Business%20Meeting%2011-05-15.pdf United States Senate Judiciary Committee: Results of Executive Business Meeting – November 5, 2015] His nomination expired on January 3, 2017, at the end of the [[114th United States Congress|114th Congress]]. ===Renomination to district court under Trump=== In August 2017, Brown was one of several candidates pitched by the White House to U.S. Senators from New York [[Chuck Schumer]] and [[Kirsten Gillibrand]] for judicial candidates for vacancies on the federal courts in New York.{{Cite web |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/zoetillman/the-white-house-has-pitched-a-nominee-for-manhattans |title=The White House Has Pitched A Nominee For Manhattan's Powerful US Attorney Opening |last=Tillman |first=Zoe |date=August 7, 2017 |publisher=[[BuzzFeed]] |access-date=May 10, 2018}} On May 10, 2018, President [[Donald Trump]] announced his intent to nominate Brown to serve as a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] for the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York]]. His nomination was part of a bipartisan package of judicial nominees which included [[Eric Komitee]], [[Rachel Kovner]], [[John Sinatra]], and [[Mary Kay Vyskocil]].https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/presidential-actions/president-donald-j-trump-announces-fourteenth-wave-judicial-nominees-thirteenth-wave-united-states-attorney-nominees-eighth-wave-united-states-marshal-nominees/ On May 15, 2018, his nomination was sent to the [[United States Senate|Senate]]. He was renominated to the same seat. On September 13, 2018, his nomination was reported out of committee by a 21–0 vote.[https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/09-13-18%20Results%20of%20Executive%20Business%20Meeting.pdf Results of Executive Business Meeting – September 13, 2018 Senate Judiciary Committee] On January 3, 2019, his nomination was returned to the President under [[Standing Rules of the United States Senate, Rule XXXI|Rule XXXI, Paragraph 6]] of the [[United States Senate]].{{cite news |title=Trump Drops Obama Picks, N.Y., Calif. Names From Judges List |url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/us-law-week/trump-drops-obama-picks-n-y-calif-names-from-judges-list-1 |access-date=15 February 2019 |publisher=Bloomberg Law |date=January 23, 2019}} On April 8, 2019, President Trump announced the renomination of Brown to the district court.[https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/presidential-actions/president-donald-j-trump-announces-judicial-nominations/ "President Donald J. Trump Announces Judicial Nominations", White House, April 8, 2019] On May 21, 2019, his nomination was sent to the Senate.[https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/presidential-actions/twelve-nominations-sent-senate-3/ "Twelve Nominations Sent to the Senate", The White House, May 21, 2019] On June 20, 2019, his nomination was reported out of committee by a [[voice vote]].[https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/Results%20of%20Executive%20Business%20Meeting%20June%2020%202019.pdf Results of Executive Business Meeting – June 20, 2019, Senate Judiciary Committee] On December 18, 2019, the Senate invoked [[cloture]] on his nomination by a 91–2 vote.{{Cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=116&session=1&vote=00411|title=On the Cloture Motion (Motion to Invoke Cloture: Gary Richard Brown to be U.S. District Judge for the Eastern District of New York)|website=www.senate.gov|access-date=2019-12-19}} On December 19, 2019, his nomination was confirmed by a [[voice vote]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov/nomination/116th-congress/773|title=PN773 — Gary Richard Brown — The Judiciary 116th Congress (2019-2020)|website=www.congress.gov|access-date=June 27, 2023}} He received his judicial commission on December 31, 2019.{{FJC Bio|nid=7545476|inline=yes}} ===Notable cases=== In December 2025, Brown ordered ICE to provide photos of a holding cell, which was described as "putrid and cramped". Brown slammed ICE for refusing to comply with his order and turn over photos. Brown also found over falsehoods in ICE's reports, such as its claims that a defendant was moved between facilities that are more than 20 miles apart and require “a drive of 35 minutes or more" in just 8 minutes.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/trump-judge-rips-ice-for-evasive-and-demonstrably-false-claims/|title=Trump Judge Gives ICE an Ultimatum Over ‘Demonstrably False’ Claims|website=Daily Beast|date=2025-12-22|access-date=2025-12-26}} ==Other interests== Brown has had a long time interest in [[magic (illusion)|magic]], which he began performing at the age of seven. Besides many contributions to magic periodicals and websites, he authored the book ''The Coney Island Fakir'' (1997), a biography about magician [[Al Flosso]]; and ''Wandcraft: Making and Using a Magic Wand'' (2020).Brown, Judge Gary. "About the Author" in ''Wandcraft: Making and Using a Magic Wand'', p.88. Theory and Art of Magic Press, Memphis, 2020. He has appeared on television as a commentator on magic numerous times, and has frequently delivered lectures for magic organizations. In 2020 he received the "Heroism and Patriot Award" from the Society of American Magicians.[https://www.judgebrownmagic.com/about Meet Judge Brown], originally published in ''The Linking Ring'' (October 2020). Retrieved 22 May 2021. Brown has also invented several magical effects, including the Viking "Spirit Trumpet" and "Telekinetic Chess" illusions.[https://geniimagazine.com/wiki/index.php?title=Judge_Gary_Brown Judge Gary Brown], ''Magicpedia''. Retrieved 22 May 2021. Judge Brown was recently on The [[CW network]] show, ''Penn & Teller Fool Us'', aired 3-31-2023. [[Harvard Law School|Harvard University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) | footnotes = }} '''Geoffrey William Crawford''' (born July 20, 1954) is a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Vermont]] and former associate justice of the [[Vermont Supreme Court]]. ==Biography== Crawford was born in 1954 in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.vermontjudiciary.org/Lists/JusticeBios/DispForm.aspx?ID=5|title=Official Biography at Vermont Judiciary|publisher=|access-date=2014-05-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521032457/https://www.vermontjudiciary.org/Lists/JusticeBios/DispForm.aspx?ID=5|archive-date=2014-05-21|url-status=dead}} He received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree, cum laude, in 1977 from [[Yale University]]. He received a [[Juris Doctor]], cum laude, in 1980 from [[Harvard Law School]]. He began his legal career as a [[law clerk]] to Judge [[Albert Wheeler Coffrin]] of the United States District Court for the District of Vermont from 1980 to 1981. From 1981 to 1984, he was an associate at the law firm of Burlingham, Underwood & Lord in [[New York City]] and from 1984 to 1987, he was an associate at the law firm of Manchester & O'Neill in [[Vermont]]. From 1987 to 2002, he was a partner with [[Jerome O'Neill]] at the law firm of O'Neil, Crawford & Green.{{cite news |last=Donoghue |first=Mike |date=March 24, 2014 |title=Crawford recommended for judgeship on Vermont's U.S. District Court |url=https://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/news/local/2014/03/24/crawford-recommended-for-judgeship-on-vermonts-us-district-court/6832271/ |work=[[The Burlington Free Press]] |location=Burlington, VT |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} He served as a judge of the [[Judiciary of Vermont|Vermont Superior Court]] from 2002 to 2013. In 2013 he succeeded [[Brian L. Burgess]] as an associate justice of the [[Vermont Supreme Court]], and he served until 2014.{{cite news |last=Zind |first=Steve |date=September 20, 2013 |title=Judge Geoffrey Crawford Appointed To Vermont Supreme Court |url=http://digital.vpr.net/post/judge-geoffrey-crawford-appointed-vermont-supreme-court |work=Vermont Public Radio |location=Colchester, VT}}{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2014/05/19/president-obama-announces-intent-nominate-justice-geoffrey-w-crawford-se|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=President Obama Announces Intent to Nominate Justice Geoffrey W. Crawford to Serve on the United States District Court for the District of Vermont|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=19 May 2014}}{{FJC Bio|nid=1394596|inline=yes}} ===Federal judicial service=== On May 20, 2014, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Crawford to serve as a United States district judge of the United States District Court for the District of Vermont, to the seat being vacated by Judge [[William K. Sessions III]], who subsequently assumed [[senior status]] on June 15, 2014. Crawford was recommended to President Obama, on March 24, 2014, by Senator [[Patrick J. Leahy]] after being evaluated by a nonpartisan Judicial Selection Commission established by Senator Leahy and Senator [[Bernie Sanders]].{{cite web|url=http://www.leahy.senate.gov/press/leahy-recommends-vermont-supreme-court-justice-geoffrey-crawford-for-vermonts-upcoming-us-district-court-vacancy|title=Leahy Recommends Vermont Supreme Court Justice Geoffrey Crawford For Vermont's Upcoming U.S. District Court Vacancy – U.S. Senator Patrick Leahy of Vermont|website=www.leahy.senate.gov}} A hearing on his nomination before the [[United States Senate Judiciary Committee]] was held on June 4, 2014.{{cite web|title=June 4, 2014: Judicial Nominations|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/meetings/judicial-nominations-2014-06-04|publisher=United States Senate}} On June 12, 2014 his nomination was reported out of committee by a [[voice vote]].{{cite web|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/Results%20of%20Executive%20Business%20Meeting%20-%2006-12-14.pdf|title=Executive Business Meeting|publisher=Committee on the Judiciary|work=United States Senate| date=12 June 2014}} On June 19, 2014 [[Senate Majority Leader]] [[Harry Reid]] filed a motion to invoke [[cloture]] on the nomination. On June 23, 2014, the [[United States Senate]] invoked [[cloture]] on his nomination by a 52–32 vote.{{cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=113&session=2&vote=00205|title=On the Cloture Motion (Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Nomination of Geoffrey Crawford, of Vermont, to be U.S. District Judge)|publisher=United States Senate|access-date=24 June 2014}} On June 24, 2014, his nomination was confirmed by a 95–0 vote.{{cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=113&session=2&vote=00209|title=On the Nomination (Confirmation Geoffrey W. Crawford, of Vermont, to be U.S. District Judge)|publisher=United States Senate|access-date=24 June 2014}} He received his judicial commission on August 4, 2014. He took the oath of office during his judicial investiture ceremony on August 12, 2014, and he maintained chambers in the United States Courthouse in [[Rutland (city), Vermont|Rutland]], [[Vermont]].[http://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/news/local/vermont/2014/08/12/crawford-officially-sworn-federal-judge/13973843/ "Crawford Official Sworn in as Federal Judge" Burlington Free Press, August 13, 2014] [[Harold Eaton Jr.]] succeed him on the Vermont Supreme Court.{{cite news |last=VTD Staff|date=October 13, 2014|title=Shumlin appoints Windsor judge to Supreme Court|url=https://vtdigger.org/2014/10/13/shumlin-appoints-windsor-judge-supreme-court/#.WhVsdaLXuEg |work=VT Digger|location=Montpelier, VT}} He served as chief judge from 2017 to 2024.[http://www.vtd.uscourts.gov/sites/vtd/files/Notice.NewChiefJudge.Crawford.pdf "Notice of New Chief Judge", District of Vermont, December 21, 2017] He assumed [[senior status]] on August 9, 2024. On April 30, he ordered the release of [[Detention of Mohsen Mahdawi|Mohsen Mahdawi]], a Palestinian student at Columbia University [[Visa and deportation controversies in the second Trump administration|detained]] under the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]], stating that "the two weeks of detention so far demonstrate great harm to a person who has been charged with no crime."{{Cite news |last=Betts |first=Anna |date=2025-04-30 |title=Federal judge in Vermont orders release of Columbia student Mohsen Mahdawi |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/apr/30/mohsen-mahdawi-released-immigration-detention |access-date=2025-04-30 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{Cite news |last=Martínez-Beltrán |first=Sergio |date=2025-04-30 |title=Federal judge orders release of Columbia University student Mohsen Mahdawi |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/04/30/nx-s1-5382306/mohsen-madawi-released-ice-columbia-university-activist-judge |access-date=2025-04-30 |work=NPR |language=en}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1394596}} *{{Ballotpedia|Geoffrey_Crawford}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[William K. [[Harvard Law School|Harvard University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''George Augustine O'Toole Jr.'''{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=379B6VwB1FMC&pg=PA697|page=697|title=Hearings before the Committee on the Judiciary, United States Senate, One Hundred Fourth Congress, First Session, on Confirmations of Appointees to the Federal Judiciary, February 8, 27; March 28; May 4; June 6 and 27, 1995|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office|year=1996}} (born October 7, 1947) is an American lawyer and jurist serving as a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts]]. == Education and career == Born in [[Worcester, Massachusetts]], O'Toole received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] from [[Boston College]] in 1969 and a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[Harvard Law School]] in 1972. He was in private practice in [[Boston, Massachusetts]] from 1972 to 1982. He was an associate justice of the [[Boston Municipal Court]] from 1982 to 1990, and of the Superior Court of Massachusetts from 1990 to 1995. == Federal judicial service == On April 4, 1995, O'Toole was nominated by President [[Bill Clinton]] to a new seat on the [[United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts]] created by 104 Stat. 5089 following the appointment of [[Rya W. Zobel]] as director of the [[Federal Judicial Center]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on May 25, 1995, and received his commission on May 26, 1995. He assumed [[senior status]] on January 1, 2018. === Notable decision === O'Toole presided over the 2015 trial of [[Dzhokhar Tsarnaev]], one of the perpetrators of the [[Boston Marathon bombing]].[https://www.cnn.com/2015/01/02/us/boston-marathon-bombing-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-trial/ Boston Marathon Bombing] ''CNN''. January 2, 2015.[https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-30680319 Boston bombing: Jury selection begins in Tsarnaev case] ''BBC''. January 6, 2015. Retrieved January 8, 2015. On February 6, 2025, O'Toole temporarily blocked the [[U.S. federal deferred resignation program]].{{Cite web|last1=Charalambous|first1=Peter|url=https://abcnews.com/US/judge-request-block-trumps-federal-government-employee-buyout/story?id=118535508|title= Judge temporarily blocks Trump's federal government employee buyout|date=February 6, 2025|website=ABC News}} On February 12, 2025, he allowed the reauthorization of the program.{{Cite web |last=Gulla |first=Erin Mulvaney and Gretchen Tarrant |title=Judge Lifts Freeze on Trump’s Buyout Plan for Federal Workers |url=https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/judge-lifts-freeze-on-trumps-buyout-plan-for-federal-workers-fb3592f5?mod=hp_lead_pos3#comments_sector |access-date=2025-02-12 |website=WSJ |language=en-US}} == Personal life == He is married to Lucy A. Flynn, a local banker, businesswoman,[https://www.jdjournal.com/2014/12/26/boston-bomber-judge-has-tough-reputation/] JD Journal, December 26, 2014. and community activist. [[University of Maryland, Baltimore]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''George Levi Russell III''' (born 1965) is the [[Chief District Judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Maryland]]. ==Biography== George Levi Russell III was born in 1965 in [[Baltimore]], Maryland.{{cite web|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/nominations/112thCongressJudicialNominations/upload/GeorgeRussell-PublicQuestionnaire.pdf|title=Senate Judiciary Committee Questionnaire|publisher=|access-date=2012-02-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120526150300/http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/nominations/112thCongressJudicialNominations/upload/GeorgeRussell-PublicQuestionnaire.pdf|archive-date=2012-05-26|url-status=dead}} His father, George Levi Russell Jr. (1929–2025), was the first African American to sit on the circuit court in Maryland.{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Cayla |title=George Russell, Baltimore judge who broke racial barriers, dies at 96 |url=https://www.thebaltimorebanner.com/obituaries/george-russell-judge-circuit-court-baltimore-XVJZSVQ7MVGJVHSUBMHOHKGNKE/ |access-date=April 14, 2025 |work=[[The Baltimore Banner]] |date=April 14, 2025 |language=en}} Russell received his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[Morehouse College]] in 1988. He received his [[Juris Doctor]] from the [[University of Maryland School of Law]] in 1991. He served as a law clerk for Judge [[Robert M. Bell]] of the [[Maryland Court of Appeals]] from 1991 to 1992. He worked at Hazel & Thomas PC from 1992 to 1994. He served as an [[Assistant United States Attorney]] from 1994 to 1999 handling civil matters. He worked at the law firm of Peter G. Angelos, PC from 2000 to 2002. He again served as an Assistant United States Attorney from 2002 to 2007 handling criminal cases. He was appointed as an associate judge of the Circuit Court of Maryland in Baltimore where he served from 2007 until 2012.{{cite web | url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2011/11/10/president-obama-nominates-four-serve-us-district-court-bench | title = President Obama Nominates Four to Serve on the US District Court Bench | author = Office of the Press Secretary | date = 10 November 2011 | via=[[NARA|National Archives]] | work=[[whitehouse.gov]] | access-date = 11 November 2011}}{{FJC Bio|nid=1393981|inline=yes}} ===Federal judicial service=== On November 10, 2011, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Russell to be a district judge on the United States District Court for the District of Maryland. He would replace Judge [[Peter J. Messitte]], who assumed senior status in 2008. He received his [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|Senate Judiciary Committee]] hearing on January 26, 2012 and his nomination was reported to the floor on February 16, 2012 by [[voice vote]], with Senator [[Mike Lee]] recording the only no vote. On May 14, 2012, the Senate confirmed his nomination by [[voice vote]]. He received his commission on May 22, 2012. Russell became the chief judge on May 1, 2024, after [[James K. Bredar]] assumed [[senior status]].{{Cite web|date=October 12, 2023|title=Chief Judge James K. Bredar to Assume Senior Status on April 30, 2024|url=https://www.mdd.uscourts.gov/news/chief-judge-james-k-bredar-assume-senior-status-april-30-2024-2023-10-12t000000|website=mdd.uscourts.gov|access-date=October 13, 2023|archive-date=October 17, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231017122438/https://www.mdd.uscourts.gov/news/chief-judge-james-k-bredar-assume-senior-status-april-30-2024-2023-10-12t000000|url-status=live}}{{Cite press release |title=Chief Judge Transition |date=May 1, 2024 |publisher=United States District Court for the District of Maryland |url=https://www.mdd.uscourts.gov/news/chief-judge-transition-2024-05-01t000000 |access-date=May 1, 2024}} == See also == * [[List of African-American federal judges]] * [[List of African-American jurists]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1393981}} *{{Ballotpedia|George_L._Russell,_III}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[Peter J. '''George Michael Marovich''' (born January 2, 1931) is an [[Senior Status|inactive senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois]].<ref>{{cite book |title={{as written|Comfir|mation [sic]}} Hearings On Federal Appointments |date=1989 |publisher=the Library of Congress |page=579 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P0ITAAAAIAAJ&q=George+M.+Marovich+1931 |access-date=25 March 2021}}</ref>

==Education and career==

Marovich was born in [[East Hazel Crest, Illinois]]. He received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1952, where he was a member of [[Tau Kappa Epsilon]] fraternity, and a [[Juris Doctor]] from the [[University of Illinois College of Law]] in 1954.<ref>{{cite magazine |date=December 1989 |title=With the Alumni |url=https://my.tke.org/theteke/Vol.%2082,%20No.%202%20PDF.pdf |magazine=The Teke |publisher=[[Tau Kappa Epsilon]] |volume=82 |issue=2 |page=30 |access-date=July 21, 2024}}</ref> He was a title examiner for the Chicago Title and Trust Company in [[Chicago]], Illinois from 1954 to 1959. He was in private practice in [[South Holland, Illinois]] from 1959 to 1966. He was a vice president & trust officer for South Holland Trust & Savings Bank of South Holland from 1966 to 1976. He was a judge of the Criminal Division of the Circuit Court of [[Cook County, Illinois|Cook County]], Illinois from 1976 to 1985. He was a judge of the Chancery Division of the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois from 1985 to 1988.<ref name="fjc.gov">{{FJC Bio|nid=1384321|inline=yes}}</ref>

===Federal judicial service===

Marovich was nominated by President [[Ronald Reagan]] on February 2, 1988, to a seat on the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois]] vacated by Judge [[Susan Christine O'Meara Getzendanner]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on March 31, 1988, and received his commission on April 1, 1988. He assumed [[senior status]] on January 2, 2000. He is currently{{when?|date=April 2024}} in inactive senior status, which means that he no longer hears cases or participates in the business of the court.<ref name="fjc.gov"/>

[[University of Pennsylvania Law School|University of Pennsylvania]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) | occupation = | profession = | known_for = | salary = | net_worth = | cabinet = | committees = | portfolio = | awards = | signature = | signature_alt = | website = | footnotes = }} '''Gerald Austin McHugh Jr.''' (born 1954) is a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania]]. ==Biography== McHugh was born and raised in [[West Philadelphia]]. McHugh received an [[Bachelor of Arts|Artium Baccalaureus]] degree, ''summa cum laude'', in 1976 from [[St. Joseph's University]]. He received a [[Juris Doctor]], ''cum laude'', in 1979 from the [[University of Pennsylvania Law School]]. In 1979, he served as a [[law clerk]] to Judge Edmund B. Spaeth of the [[Pennsylvania Superior Court]]. From 1979 to 1981, he served as a law clerk to Judge [[Alfred Leopold Luongo]] of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. From 1981 to 2004, he was a [[shareholder]] at the civil litigation law firm of Litvin, Blumberg, Matusow and Young. From 2004 to 2014, he was a partner at the [[Philadelphia]] law firm of Raynes McCarty, where he handled complex [[civil litigation]] involving [[tort]], [[insurance law|insurance]], and [[civil rights law|civil rights claims]].{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2013/08/01/president-obama-nominates-six-serve-united-states-district-courts|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=President Obama Nominates Six to Serve on the United States District Courts|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=1 August 2013}}{{FJC Bio|nid=1394421|inline=yes}} ===Federal judicial service=== On August 1, 2013, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated McHugh to serve as a United States district judge of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, to the seat vacated by Judge [[Harvey Bartle III]], who assumed [[senior status]] on October 1, 2011. On January 16, 2014 his nomination was reported out of committee by a 12–5 vote.{{cite web|title=Executive Business Meeting|url=https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/ExecutiveBusinessMeetingResults-01-16-2014.pdf|work=United States Senate|publisher=Committee on the Judiciary|access-date=16 January 2014}} On Thursday March 13, 2014 [[Harry Reid|Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid]] filed a motion to invoke [[cloture]] on the nomination. On March 26, 2014, the [[United States Senate]] invoked cloture on his nomination by a 56–43 vote.{{cite web|title=On the Cloture Motion (Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Nomination of Gerald McHugh, Jr., of Pennsylvania, to be U.S. District Judge)|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=113&session=2&vote=00082|publisher=United States Senate|access-date=26 March 2014}} He was confirmed later that day by a 59–41 vote.{{cite web|title=On the Nomination (Confirmation Gerald Austin McHugh, Jr., of Pennsylvania, to be U.S. District Judge)|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=113&session=2&vote=00086|publisher=United States Senate|access-date=26 March 2014}} He received his judicial commission on March 28, 2014. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1394421}} *{{Ballotpedia|Gerald_Austin_McHugh,_Jr}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[Harvey Bartle III]]}} {{s-ttl|title={{nowrap|Judge of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania]]}}|years=2014–present}} {{s-inc}} {{s-end}} {{United States 3rd Circuit district judges}} {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:McHugh, Gerald A. {{nowrap|[[University of Nevada-Reno]] (MJS)}} | alma_mater = | occupation = | profession = | known_for = | salary = | net_worth = | cabinet = | committees = | portfolio = | awards = | signature = | signature_alt = | website = | footnotes = }} '''Gershwin Allen Drain''' (born January 24, 1949) is a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan]]. ==Early life and education== Born in [[Detroit]], Gershwin A. Drain attended Detroit St. Gregory High School, a [[Catholic high school]], where he was president of his senior class.{{cite web|url=http://www.bishopgallagher.org/2012/10/judge-gershwin-drain-on-his-catholic-education.html|title=Judge Gershwin Drain on his Catholic Education – The Detroit Catholic School Heritage Project |date=October 28, 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://www.legalnews.com/detroit/1366853/|title=Drain ready to assume new role on U.S. District Court; Judge is assembling a staff and adjusting to the federal system|author=Steve Thorpe|work=Detroit Legal News |date=September 5, 2012}} He received his [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1970 from [[Western Michigan University]], which he attended on a football scholarship and for which he played football as a [[running back]] for the [[Western Michigan Broncos football|Western Michigan Broncos]] from 1968 to 1969.{{cite web|url=https://www.mied.uscourts.gov/index.cfm?pageFunction=chambers&judgeid=36|title=Judge Gershwin A. Drain|publisher=United States District Court – Eastern Michigan District}}[http://www.wmubroncos.com/pdf8/891983.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=4600 "2012 WMU Football Record Book"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001532/http://www.wmubroncos.com/pdf8/891983.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=4600 |date=March 4, 2016 }}, WMUBroncos.com{{cite web|url=http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=204953872|title=Football History: All-Time Jersey Roster: #33|work=WMUBroncos.com}} He received his [[Juris Doctor]] in 1972 from the [[University of Michigan Law School]]. In 1991, he received a Masters of Judicial Studies degree from the [[University of Nevada-Reno]].{{FJC Bio|nid=1394036|inline=yes}} ==Career== Drain served as a law clerk for the Third Circuit Court of Michigan from 1972 to 1973. He worked as counsel for the [[Detroit Department of Transportation]] from 1973 to 1974. He then worked as an attorney in the Federal Defender Office for the Eastern District of Michigan from 1974 to 1986. He represented defendants charged with criminal felonies in federal court, and tried approximately 144 cases.[http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/GershwinDrain-PublicQuestionnaire.pdf "United States Senate, Committee on the Judiciary, Questionnaire for Judicial Nominees; Public"], November 10, 2011 === State judicial service === Drain served as a judge of the 36th District Court for Detroit from 1986 to 1987. He served as a judge on the [[Recorder's Court]] for Detroit, a state criminal court, exclusively handling felony prosecution criminal cases from 1987 to 1997, at which time said court was merged with the Third Circuit Court. He served as a judge on the Third Circuit Court of Michigan from 1997 to 2012, working in both the civil and criminal divisions of the court.{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2011/11/17/president-obama-nominates-judge-gershwin-drain-serve-us-district-court|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=President Obama Nominates Judge Gershwin A. Drain to Serve on the US District Court|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=November 17, 2011}} By 2011, he had presided over approximately 600 cases that had gone to verdict or judgment. Of those, approximately 55 percent were jury trials, and 70 percent were criminal proceedings. ===Federal judicial service=== On November 17, 2011, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Drain for District Judge for the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan]]. Obama remarked: "Judge Gershwin A. Drain will bring an unwavering commitment to fairness and judicial integrity to the federal bench. His impressive legal career is a testament to the kind of thoughtful and diligent judge he will be on the U.S. District Court." He replaced Judge [[Bernard A. Friedman]], who assumed senior status in 2009.{{cite web|url=http://archive.freep.com/article/20120929/NEWS01/309290074/-Dream-come-true-for-new-U-S-judge |author=David Jesse |date= September 29, 2012|title='Dream come true' for new U.S. judge|work=Detroit Free Press}} He was rated Unanimously Qualified by the [[American Bar Association]].{{cite web|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/nominations/judicial?c=112|title=Judicial Nominations|publisher=judiciary.senate.gov}} Regarding his views on the [[death penalty]] and [[gun control]], Drain said:
The Republicans called me 'controversial' because of an anti-death penalty article I had written. I told them that I have to follow the law and apply it. I also wrote an article called 'I Have a Dream of Non-violence' in which I said critical things about the NRA. That became an issue, too. Those who hadn't said or written anything tended to go through smoothly.
On August 2, 2012, the [[United States Senate]] confirmed Drain by a 55–41 vote.{{cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=112&session=2&vote=00189|title=On the Nomination (Confirmation Gershwin A. Drain, of Michigan, to be U.S. District Judge for the Eastern District of Michigan)|date=August 12, 2014|publisher=US Senate}}{{cite web|url=http://detroit.cbslocal.com/2012/08/02/senate-confirms-wayne-county-judge-for-us-court/|title=Senate Confirms Wayne County Judge For US Court|publisher=CBS|date= August 2, 2012}} He received his judicial commission on August 8, 2012. He assumed [[senior status]] on August 13, 2022. ===Notable cases=== In November 2014, he presided over the [[immigration fraud]] trial of [[Rasmea Odeh]], and told the jury that he thought its guilty verdict was "a fair and reasonable one based on the evidence that came in."{{cite web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/wayne-county/2014/11/10/arab-activist-immigration-case-bombing/18796851/|title=Arab activist's bond revoked for immigration conviction|author=Jeff Karoub|date=November 10, 2014|work=The Detroit News}} On February 13, 2015, he denied Odeh's appeal, ruling that her argument lacked legal merit.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2015/02/16/us/ap-us-immigration-israel-bombing.html?_r=0|title=No New Trial for Arab Activist for Lying About Killing Role|work=New York Times|agency=Associated Press|date=February 16, 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.algemeiner.com/2015/02/16/judge-slams-rasmieh-odehs-request-for-new-trial/|title=Judge Slams Rasmieh Odeh's Request for New Trial|work=Algemeiner|date=February 16, 2015}} The judge held that evidence showed that Odeh illegally obtained U.S. citizenship by failing to disclose her conviction for fatal terrorist bombings, that the jurors "clearly did not believe [her] explanation", and that "the evidence was more than sufficient to support the jury's verdict." Judge Drain sentenced Odeh to 18 months in federal prison on March 12, 2015, stripping her of her [[citizenship of the United States]], and ordering her [[deportation]] at the end of her sentence.{{cite web|url=http://chicago.suntimes.com/news-chicago/7/71/434837/suburban-palestinian-immigrant-sentenced-x-years-terror-related-case|title=Suburban Palestinian immigrant sentenced to 18 months in prison in terror-related case|date=March 12, 2015|work=Chicago Sun Times|access-date=March 12, 2015|archive-date=March 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314151551/http://chicago.suntimes.com/news-chicago/7/71/434837/suburban-palestinian-immigrant-sentenced-x-years-terror-related-case|url-status=dead}} On February 25, 2016, Odeh won her appeal to the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit]].{{cite news|last1=Wisniewski|first1=Mary|title=Palestinian activist's U.S. immigration fraud conviction vacated|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-michigan-immigration-fraud-idUSKCN0VY2KU|access-date=8 December 2016|work=[[Reuters]]|date=25 February 2016}} Circuit Judge [[John M. Rogers]], joined partially by Judge [[Karen Nelson Moore]], vacated and remanded, while Judge [[Alice M. Batchelder]] partially dissented, wanting to vacate while ordering a new trial.[https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=6954439213867437073&hl=en&as_sdt=2006 ''United States v. Odeh''], 815 F.3d 968 (6th Cir. 2016). On December 6, 2016, Judge Drain denied prosecutors' request to reinstate Odeh's conviction, instead granting Odeh a new trial, scheduled to begin January 10, 2017.{{cite news|last1=Whitcomb|first1=Dan|title=U.S. judge grants new immigration fraud trial for Palestinian activist|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/michigan-immigration-fraud-idUSL1N1E12HC|access-date=8 December 2016|work=[[Reuters]]|date=6 December 2016}} On July 21, 2016, Drain struck down Michigan's ban on [[straight-ticket voting]]. He wrote that the ban would result in longer lines at polling places and would disproportionately harm black voters.https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2016/07/21/federal-judge-blocks-michigan-ban-straight-party-voting/87392104/ July 21, 2016. Retrieved February 23, 2021. ==Awards and associations== Drain is a member of the Michigan Bar Association, the Association of Black Judges of Michigan, a Prison Ministry for the [[Mound Correctional Facility]], and is a lifetime member of the [[NAACP]] since 1989. He was named "Michiganian of the Year" by the ''[[Detroit News]]'' in 1997.[http://www.detroitlawyer.org/topic.jsp?topicId=721 Judge Drain bio]{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, Detroit Metro Bar Association ==Personal life== Drain and his wife, Meredith, have two daughters, both of whom are lawyers.Kelly Rimmer (Winter 2013) [http://www.fbamich.org/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=L2-wIn6N4jQ%3D&tabid=440 "Judge Gershwin A. Drain Investiture Ceremony"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129020056/http://www.fbamich.org/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=L2-wIn6N4jQ%3D&tabid=440 |date=November 29, 2014 }}, ''FBA Newsletter'' == See also == * [[List of African-American federal judges]] * [[List of African-American jurists]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1394036}} *{{Ballotpedia|Gershwin_Drain}} *[http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/GershwinDrain-PublicQuestionnaire.pdf "United States Senate, Committee on the Judiciary, Questionnaire for Judicial Nominees; Public"], November 10, 2011 {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[Bernard A. [[West Virginia University College of Law|West Virginia University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) | footnotes = }} '''Gina Marie Groh''' (née '''Householder'''; born 1964) is an American lawyer who serves as a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of West Virginia]]. ==Early life and education== A native of Williamsport, Maryland, Groh received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree, ''[[summa cum laude]]'' from [[Shepherd University|Shepherd College]] in 1986. She received the McMurran Scholar Award, the highest academic honor granted by Shepherd.{{cite news | title = McMurran Scholars | date = May 1986 | url = http://www.shepherd.edu/aaweb/mcmurran/ | work = Shepherd University |access-date = May 27, 2011}} In 1989 she received a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[West Virginia University College of Law]].{{FJC Bio|nid=1393916|inline=yes}} ==Career== After law school, Groh worked at the law firm of Steptoe & Johnson from 1989 to 1991 and Mell, Brownell & Baker from 1991 to 1995. She took a position with the firm Semmes, Bowen & Semmes from 1995 to 1998. Groh became an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for [[Berkeley County, West Virginia]] between the years of 1998 to 2002. From 2002 until 2006, she was an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for [[Jefferson County, West Virginia]]. In 2006, she was appointed by (then) Governor [[Joe Manchin]] as a Judge of the 23rd Judicial Circuit Court of West Virginia. She was the first female Judge to serve in the 23rd Judicial Circuit and at the time of her appointment was only the third female circuit judge in West Virginia.{{cite web | url = http://www.shepherd.edu/university/features/groh/ | title = GINA M. GROH '86 NAMED THIRD FEMALE CIRCUIT JUDGE IN THE STATE | access-date = May 20, 2011 | last = Spataro | first = Jennifer | publisher = Shepherd University | archive-date = September 27, 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110927024250/http://www.shepherd.edu/university/features/groh/ | url-status = dead }}{{cite news | title = President Obama Nominates Three to the United States District Court | date = May 19, 2011 | url = https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2011/05/19/president-obama-nominates-three-united-states-district-court | work = The White House | access-date = May 20, 2011 | archive-date = April 3, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150403161831/https://m.whitehouse.gov/the-press-office/2011/05/19/president-obama-nominates-three-united-states-district-court | url-status = live }} She served as a circuit court judge from her appointment in 2006 until March 19, 2012 when she resigned in order to receive her federal judicial commission. She is the first United States District Judge from the [[Eastern Panhandle of West Virginia]]. ===Federal judicial service=== In March 2011, Senators [[Joe Manchin]] and [[Jay Rockefeller]] recommended Groh to President [[Barack Obama]] to fill a vacant seat on the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of West Virginia]].{{cite news|title=Panhandle Judge Gina Marie Groh nominated to federal bench |date=May 19, 2011 |publisher=The Associated Press |url=http://www.herald-mail.com/news/tristate/hm-panhandle-judge-gina-marie-groh-nominated-to-federal-bench-20110519,0,6399523.story |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125121613/http://www.herald-mail.com/news/tristate/hm-panhandle-judge-gina-marie-groh-nominated-to-federal-bench-20110519,0,6399523.story |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 25, 2013 |work=herald-mail.com |access-date=May 20, 2011 }} On May 19, 2011, Groh was nominated by the president to fill the seat of Judge [[W. Craig Broadwater]], who died in 2006. Her nomination was reported out of the [[Senate Judiciary Committee]] on October 6, 2011 by a [[voice vote]]. On March 15, 2012, the Senate confirmed Groh by a 95–2 vote.{{cite web|url= https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1122/vote_112_2_00049.htm|title=On the Nomination (Confirmation Gina Marie Groh, of West Virginia, to be U.S. District Judge)|access-date=November 3, 2022|date=March 15, 2012|publisher=U.S. Senate}} She received her commission on March 20, 2012. Her formal investiture ceremony took place on October 19, 2012, at [[Shepherd University]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rockefeller.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/2012/10/rockefeller-honors-judge-gina-groh-at-judicial-ceremony |title=ROCKEFELLER-HONORS-JUDGE-GINA-GROH-AT-JUDICIAL-CEREMONY |access-date=October 19, 2012 |date=October 19, 2012 |publisher=Senator Jay Rockefeller |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706195755/http://www.rockefeller.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/2012/10/rockefeller-honors-judge-gina-groh-at-judicial-ceremony |archive-date=2014-07-06 }} She served as Chief Judge from 2015 to 2022. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1393916}} *{{Ballotpedia|Gina_Marie_Groh}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[W.
