[[Columbia Law School|Columbia University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) | birth_date = 1968 }} '''Richard Franklin Boulware II''' (born 1968) is a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Nevada]] and former assistant Federal Public Defender. ==Biography== Boulware received an [[Bachelor of Arts|Artium Baccalaureus]] degree, cum laude, in 1993 from [[Harvard College]] and studied toward a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Sociology from 1995 to 1998. He received a [[Juris Doctor]] in 2002 from [[Columbia Law School]].{{Cite web |title=Judge Richard F. Boulware – District of Nevada |url=https://www.nvd.uscourts.gov/court-information/judges/judge-richard-f-boulware/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |language=en-US}} From 2002 to 2003, he served as a [[law clerk]] to Judge [[Denise Cote]] of the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York]]. From 2003 to 2007, he was a trial attorney in the [[Federal Public Defender's Office]] in [[New York City]]. He served in the Federal Public Defender's Office in [[Las Vegas]] from 2007 to 2014, serving as the lead attorney for complex white-collar cases from 2010 to 2014.{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2014/01/16/president-obama-nominates-four-serve-united-states-district-courts|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=President Obama Nominates Four to Serve on the United States District Courts|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=16 January 2014}}{{FJC Bio|nid=1394561|inline=yes}} ===Federal judicial service=== On January 16, 2014, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Boulware to serve as a district judge of the [[United States District Court for the District of Nevada]] to the seat vacated by Judge [[Philip Martin Pro]], who assumed [[senior status]] on December 31, 2011.{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2014/01/16/presidential-nominations-sent-senate|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=Presidential Nominations Sent to the Senate|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=16 January 2014}} He received a hearing before the [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary]] on March 12, 2014.{{cite web|title=Nominations|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/meetings/nominations-2014-03-12|work=United States Senate|date=12 March 2014 |publisher=Committee on the Judiciary|access-date=12 March 2014}} On April 3, 2014, his nomination was reported out of committee by a 11–7 vote.{{cite web|title=Executive Business Meeting|url=http://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/Results%20of%20Executive%20Business%20Meeting%20-%2004-03-14.pdf|work=United States Senate|publisher=Committee on the Judiciary|access-date=3 April 2014}} On June 5, 2014, Senate Majority Leader [[Harry Reid]] filed for [[cloture]] on the nomination. On June 9, 2014, the [[United States Senate]] invoked [[cloture]] by a 53–34 vote.{{cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=113&session=2&vote=00178|title=On the Cloture Motion (Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Nomination of Richard Franklin Boulware II, of Nevada, to be U.S. District Judge)|publisher=United States Senate|access-date=10 June 2014}} On June 10, 2014, his nomination was confirmed by a 58–35 vote.{{cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=113&session=2&vote=00181|title=On the Nomination (Confirmation of Richard Franklin Boulware II, of Nevada, to be United States District Judge for the District of Nevada)|publisher=United States Senate|access-date=10 June 2014}} He received his judicial commission the same day. He was sworn in on June 12, 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.nvd.uscourts.gov/Bio/rfBoulware.aspx|title=Judges List: Judge Richard F. Boulware|publisher=[[United States District Court for the District of Nevada]]|access-date=21 June 2014}} In 2015, Boulware began hearing a high-profile [[antitrust]] lawsuit against the [[UFC|Ultimate Fighting Championship]] filed by several of its former fighters. The fighters allege that the UFC "unlawfully [[monopoly|monopolized]] the market for [[mixed martial arts]] promotion by, among other things, locking up fighters with exclusive contracts and acquiring its rivals, leading to suppressed compensation for the fighters".{{cite web | url=https://www.cohenmilstein.com/case-study/mixed-martial-arts-antitrust-litigation |title=Cohen-Milstein: Mixed Martial Arts Antitrust Litigation| access-date=15 Nov 2020}} The UFC is fighting the suit, alleging that it is "meritless."{{cite web | url=https://www.bloodyelbow.com/2015/9/26/9401261/ufc-releases-statement-after-motion-dismiss-antitrust-lawsuit-denied-mma-news|title=UFC Releases Statement After Motion To Dismiss Antitrust Lawsuit Is Denied|date=26 September 2015 |access-date=15 Nov 2020}} In September 2020, Boulware indicated he was "likely" to grant class-action status to the suit.{{cite web | url=https://thebodylockmma.com/ufc/ufc-antitrust-lawsuit-granted-class-certification/ |title=UFC Antitrust Lawsuit Likely to be Granted Class Certification|date=17 September 2020 | access-date=15 Nov 2020}} In May 2022, he vacated [[Margaret Rudin]]’s murder conviction after she had spent 20 years in prison. Boulware ruled that Rudin received ineffective legal representation from her late defense attorney.{{cite web|url=https://thehill.com/news/ap/ap-u-s-news/murder-conviction-vacated-for-vegas-real-estate-moguls-wife/|title=Murder conviction vacated for Vegas real estate mogul's wife|date=May 17, 2022}} ==Nomination to United States Sentencing Commission== On September 9, 2015, President Obama nominated Boulware to a position on the [[United States Sentencing Commission]]. He would have replaced former Commissioner [[Ketanji Brown Jackson]] and his term would have expired October 31, 2019.{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/09/10/president-obama-nominates-two-serve-united-states-sentencing-commission|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|title=President Obama Nominates Two to Serve on the United States Sentencing Commission|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|date=9 September 2015}} His nomination expired at the end of the [[114th United States Congress|114th Congress]]. == See also == * [[List of African-American federal judges]] * [[List of African-American jurists]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1394561}} *{{Ballotpedia|Richard_Franklin_Boulware_II}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[Philip Martin Pro]]}} {{s-ttl|title={{nowrap|Judge of the [[United States District Court for the District of Nevada]]}}|years=2014–present}} {{s-inc}} {{s-end}} {{United States 9th Circuit district judges}} {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Boulware, Richard II}} [[Category:1968 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:African-American judges]] [[Category:Columbia Law School alumni]] [[Category:Harvard College alumni]] [[Category:Judges of the United States District Court for the District of Nevada]] [[Category:New York (state) lawyers]] [[Category:Nevada lawyers]] [[Category:People from Rochester, Minnesota]] [[Category:Public defenders]] [[Category:United States district court judges appointed by Barack Obama]]

'''Richard Mark Gergel''' (born August 14, 1954) is an American lawyer who serves as a [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of South Carolina]].

== Early life and education ==

Gergel was born in [[Columbia, South Carolina]], to Melvin and Meri ({{née|Friedman}}) Gergel, who were both children of [[Jewish]] immigrants.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Waites |first1=Robin |title=Jewish Heritage Collection: Oral history interview with Richard Gergel and Belinda Friedman Gergel |url=https://lcdl.library.cofc.edu/lcdl/catalog/246433 |website=Lowcountry Digital Library |date=2016 |access-date=29 July 2026}}</ref> Gergel earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[Duke University]] in 1975 and a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[Duke University School of Law]] in 1979.<ref name=whgov_20091222>[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/president-obama-nominates-judge-j-michelle-childs-richard-mark-gergel-district-cour President Obama Nominates Judge J. Michelle Childs, Richard Mark Gergel to District Court Bench for the District of South Carolina] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216173409/https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/president-obama-nominates-judge-j-michelle-childs-richard-mark-gergel-district-cour |date=February 16, 2017 }}, ''[[whitehouse.gov]]'' (December 22, 2009).</ref><ref name=gergel_gnslaw_bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.gnslaw.com/Bio/RichardGergel.asp|title=Richard Mark Gergel Biography – Gergel Nickles & Solomon Attorneys At Law|access-date=February 28, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100211142528/http://www.gnslaw.com/Bio/RichardGergel.asp|archive-date=February 11, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> Gergel's cousin was well-known industrial chemist [[Max Gergel]], President/CEO of the Columbia Organic Chemical Company, or COCC.<ref name="fjc.gov">{{FJC Bio|nid=1393296|inline=yes}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

From 1979 until 1980, Gergel served as a [[law clerk]] for a law firm in Columbia, South Carolina, and he was a partner with the firm from 1981 until 1982. Beginning in 1983 and continuing until his nomination to the district court, he was the president and partner with his own law firm (most recently known as Gergel, Nickles and Solomon) in Columbia. He has specialized in [[personal injury law]].<ref name="fjc.gov"/>

===Notable case===

In 1994, Gergel was the attorney representing the South Carolina Education Association and public school teacher Maggi Smith Hall. The case went to the [[Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals]] in [[Richmond, VA]], and was considered one of the most important [[First Amendment]] cases to come down from the 4th Circuit in over a decade. At the time, the 4th Circuit was also considered to be the most conservative court in the nation. (Laura Sullivan, ''[[Baltimore Sun]]'', November 18, 2003)

The case, ''Hall v. Marion School District 2,'' 31 F.3d 183 (4th Cir. 1994), upheld the lower court's decision that Mullins District 2 acted illegally in firing Hall for exercising free speech in criticizing her superintendent and school board for reckless spending.

=== Federal judicial service ===

On December 22, 2009, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Gergel to serve on the United States District Court for the District of South Carolina to fill the seat vacated by Judge [[Henry Michael Herlong, Jr.]], who assumed [[senior status]] on June 1, 2009.<ref name=whgov_20091222/><ref name="fjc.gov"/><ref>[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/presidential-nominations-sent-senate-122209 Presidential Nominations Sent to the Senate, 12/22/09], ''[[whitehouse.gov]]'' (December 22, 2009).</ref> In his questionnaire to the [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary]], Gergel wrote that South Carolina Democratic Congressmen [[John M. Spratt, Jr.]] and [[Jim Clyburn]] both previously had recommended Gergel to Obama as a district court nominee, and that South Carolina Republican Sen. [[Lindsey Graham]] also supported the nomination. Gergel had a hearing before the [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary]] on April 16, 2010. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on August 5, 2010,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.libertyfellowshipsc.org/news/columbians-gergel-childs-confirmed-federal-judges|title=Columbians Gergel, Childs Confirmed as Federal Judges|last=Monk|first=John|date=August 6, 2010|website=www.libertyfellowshipsc.org|publisher=The State|access-date=July 18, 2019|archive-date=July 18, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190718204010/https://www.libertyfellowshipsc.org/news/columbians-gergel-childs-confirmed-federal-judges|url-status=dead}}</ref> and received commission on August 9, 2010.<ref name="fjc.gov"/>

==== Trial of Dylann Roof ====
{{main|Trial of Dylann Roof}}

Gergel was the presiding judge on the trial of [[Dylann Roof]], who was convicted of 33 federal charges relating to the 2015 [[Charleston church shooting]]. Roof was convicted on all charges and controversially represented himself during the sentencing phase despite Gergel warning Roof it was not in his best interests to do so. On January 11, 2017, Gergel sentenced Dylann Roof to death after the jury recommended the [[death penalty]] the previous day.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/01/10/us/dylann-roof-trial-charleston.html|title=Dylann Roof Is Sentenced to Death in Charleston Church Massacre|last1=Blinder|first1=Alan|date=January 10, 2017|work=The New York Times|access-date=July 18, 2019|last2=Sack|first2=Kevin|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Author ==
Gergel is the author of ''Unexampled Courage: The Blinding of Sgt. Isaac Woodard and the Awakening of President Harry S. Leon''' (born December 3, 1949) is an American jurist who serves as a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia|U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia]]. He was appointed in 2002 by President [[George W. Bush]] and assumed senior status in 2016. ==Early life and education== Leon was born in [[Natick, Massachusetts|South Natick]], [[Massachusetts]], on December 3, 1949.{{Cite web |last=admin |title=Richard J. Leon |url=https://dcchs.org/judges/leon-richard-j/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=Historical Society of the D.C. Circuit |language=en-US}} His parents were Silvano B. Leon and Rita M. O'Rorke.{{cite web|url=http://www.currentobituary.com/member/obit/186238|title=Rita M. Leon|publisher=CurrentObituary.com}} His paternal grandparents were immigrants from [[Portugal]] who settled in [[Framingham, Massachusetts]].{{cite census|url=https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:K4FX-73F|title=Armando Leon|year=1940|location=Framingham, MA}} Leon graduated from the [[College of the Holy Cross]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in psychology in 1971. As an undergraduate at Holy Cross, he was a member of the school's student judicial board,{{Cite web |date=1971|title=The Class of 1971: Seniors|url=https://crossworks.holycross.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1054&context=purple_patcher|access-date=17 May 2026|website=Purple Patcher|publisher=[[College of the Holy Cross]]}} and was a classmate of [[Clarence Thomas]].{{Cite web |title=Five Outstanding Alumni Receive Sanctae Crucis Awards {{!}} Holy Cross Magazine |url=https://magazine.holycross.edu/stories/five-outstanding-alumni-receive-sanctae-crucis-awards |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=magazine.holycross.edu |language=en}} He then earned his [[Juris Doctor]] (J.D.), ''[[cum laude]]'', from the [[Suffolk University Law School]] in 1974 and earned a [[Master of Laws]] (LL.M.) from [[Harvard Law School]] in 1981.{{Cite web |title=Senior Judge Richard J. Leon {{!}} District of Columbia {{!}} United States District Court |url=https://www.dcd.uscourts.gov/content/senior-judge-richard-j-leon |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=www.dcd.uscourts.gov}} ==Legal career== Leon served as a [[law clerk]] to the justices of the [[Massachusetts Superior Court]] from 1974 to 1975 and to Thomas F. Kelleher of the [[Rhode Island Supreme Court]] from 1975 to 1976. Leon was an attorney for the [[Immigration and Naturalization Service]] of the [[United States Department of Justice]] from 1976 to 1977 and a Special [[Assistant United States Attorney]] in the office of the United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York working in the [[United States Department of Justice Civil Division|Civil Division]] from 1977 to 1978. Leon was an assistant professor of law at [[St. John's University School of Law]] from 1979 to 1983 and a senior trial attorney in the United States Department of Justice from 1983 to 1987. Leon served as deputy chief minority counsel on the Select Committee to Investigate Covert Arms Transactions with Iran of the [[United States House of Representatives]], which investigated the [[Iran-Contra affair]], from 1987 to 1988.{{FJC Bio|nid=1391441|inline=yes}} Leon was appointed Deputy [[United States Assistant Attorney General|Assistant Attorney General]] and served from 1988 to 1989, when he entered [[Practice of law|private practice]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], first with [[Baker Hostetler|Baker & Hostetler]] from 1989 to 1999 and then with [[Vorys, Sater, Seymour and Pease]] from 1999 to 2002, when he was appointed to the district court. Leon was a member of the [[White House Fellows|President's Commission on White House Fellowships]] from 1990 to 1993. Leon was appointed chief minority counsel on the [[House October Surprise Task Force|October Surprise Task Force]] of the [[United States House Committee on Foreign Affairs|House Foreign Affairs Committee]] from 1992 to 1993. He served as special counsel to the [[United States House Committee on Financial Services|House Financial Services Committee]] in 1994. He is an adjunct professor at [[The George Washington University Law School]] and the [[Georgetown University Law Center]]. ==Federal judicial service== Leon was nominated to the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]] by [[George W. Bush]] on September 10, 2001, to the seat vacated by [[Norma Holloway Johnson]]. [[Advice and consent|Confirmed]] by the [[United States Senate|Senate]] on February 14, 2002, he received his [[Letters patent|judicial commission]] five days later. He assumed [[senior status]] on December 31, 2016. ===''WilmerHale v. Executive Office of the President'' (2025)=== On May 27, 2025, Judge Leon ruled in ''WilmerHale v. Executive Office of the President'', striking down Executive Order 14250 issued by President Donald J. Trump. The order targeted the law firm WilmerHale due to its association with former Special Counsel Robert S. Mueller III. It directed federal agencies to suspend the firm’s security clearances, restrict access to federal buildings, and review existing contracts. Judge Leon found the order to be retaliatory and unconstitutional, violating the First and Fifth Amendments. In a 73-page opinion, he wrote, “The cornerstone of the American system of justice is an independent judiciary and an independent bar willing to tackle unpopular cases, however daunting.”{{cite news |last=Montague |first=Zach |title=Judge Strikes Down Trump Order Targeting WilmerHale |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/27/us/politics/trump-law-firms-wilmerhale.html |work=The New York Times |date=May 27, 2025 |access-date=May 27, 2025}}{{cite court |title=Memorandum Opinion, WilmerHale v. Executive Office of the President |url=https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.278933/gov.uscourts.dcd.278933.111.0_1.pdf |publisher=U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia |date=May 27, 2025 |access-date=May 27, 2025}} ===Guantanamo Bay=== Leon was responsible for adjudicating the [[habeas corpus]] petitions of several dozen captives held at the [[Guantanamo Bay detention camp]].{{cite web| url=http://www.pegc.us/archive/OK_v_Bush/govt_resp_to_GK_20060815.pdf| title=Respondents' response to Court's August 7, 2006 order| date=August 15, 2006| publisher=[[United States Department of Defense]]| access-date=2008-06-23| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080902020528/http://www.pegc.us/archive/OK_v_Bush/govt_resp_to_GK_20060815.pdf| archive-date=2008-09-02| url-status=live}}{{cite news| url=http://listproc.ucdavis.edu/archives/law-lib/law-lib.log0701/att-0174/01-GITMO_AttyList.pdf| title=Lead Petitioners' Counsel in Guantanamo Habeas Cases| publisher=[[Center for Constitutional Rights]]| date=January 8, 2007| access-date=2008-06-11| archive-date=2009-03-27| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090327090516/http://listproc.ucdavis.edu/archives/law-lib/law-lib.log0701/att-0174/01-GITMO_AttyList.pdf| url-status=live}}{{cite news| url=http://www.pegc.us/archive/In_re_Gitmo/gov_mot_to_dismiss_20070419.pdf| title=Exhibit B: List Of Enemy Combatant Detainees With Pending Habeas Corpus Petitions Who Have Been Released From United States Custody| pages=60–62| publisher=[[United States Department of Justice]]| date=April 17, 2007| access-date=2008-05-05| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090327090515/http://www.pegc.us/archive/In_re_Gitmo/gov_mot_to_dismiss_20070419.pdf| url-status=live| archive-date = 2009-03-27}} ''[[Boumediene v. Bush]]'', which was eventually considered by the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]], was first heard by Leon. By August 28, 2008, Leon had 24 cases assigned to him.{{cite news |last=Apuzzo |first=Matt |url=http://ap.google.com/article/ALeqM5gUxng-zkl2uhqdCATFQyY9_8QV3QD92QQ83O9 |title=Judge fears secret hearings over Guantanamo Bay |publisher=Associated Press |date=August 28, 2008 |access-date=2013-12-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080901171816/http://ap.google.com/article/ALeqM5gUxng-zkl2uhqdCATFQyY9_8QV3QD92QQ83O9 |archive-date=September 1, 2008 }} The Associated Press reported Leon hoped to resolve those cases before the [[United States presidential inauguration|presidential inauguration]] in 2009 and was concerned that the public and the detainees will be barred from observing the hearings: "If it can't be done, I have great concern that these hearings will be virtually or exclusively classified, closed to the public and, I might add, to the detainees."{{cite news|url=https://archive.boston.com/news/nation/washington/articles/2008/08/28/us_judge_voices_fear_public_will_be_shut_out_of_detainee_trials/|title=US judge voices fear public will be shut out of detainee trials|first=Matt|last=Apuzzo|agency=Associated Press|date=August 28, 2008|website=Boston.com}} During a hearing on October 23, 2008, Leon commented on the ambiguity of the term "[[enemy combatant]]" and criticized Congress and the Supreme Court: "We are here today, much to my dismay, I might add, to deal with a legal question that in my judgment should have been resolved a long time ago. I don't understand, I really don't, how the Supreme Court made the decision it made and left that question open... I don't understand how the Congress could let it go this long without resolving."{{cite news|url=http://archive.boston.com/news/nation/washington/articles/2008/10/24/lawyers_debate_enemy_combatant/ |title=Lawyers debate 'enemy combatant' |work=The Boston Globe |date=2008-10-24 |access-date=2013-12-17}} On November 20, Leon ordered [[Algerian Six|five detainees]] released from [[Guantanamo Bay Naval Base]] due to insufficient evidence.{{cite web|last=Denniston |first=Lyle |url=http://www.scotusblog.com/wp/judge-orders-five-detainees-freed/ |title=Judge orders five detainees freed |publisher=SCOTUSblog |date=2008-11-20 |access-date=2013-12-17}}{{cite web|url=https://www.salon.com/2008/11/20/guantanamo_2/ |title=Glenn Greenwald |work=[[Salon (website)|Salon]] |date=11 December 2007 |archive-date=11 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111065646/http://www.salon.com/2008/11/20/guantanamo_2/ |url-status=live |access-date=2013-12-17}} In December 2008, Leon denied [[Moath Hamza Ahmed al Alawi]]'s habeas corpus petition, finding the enemy combatant's detention was lawful under the [[Authorization for Use of Military Force of 2001]].{{Bluebook journal |first=|last=Note|title=Recent Case: D.C. Supp. 2d|opinion=24|court=D.D.C.|date=2008|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=13502220196614458634 }} In February 2017, Leon denied another habeas corpus petition from al Alawi, rejecting the detainee's claim that the war's hostilities had ceased.{{cite court |litigants=Al-Alwi v. Circuit]].{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/story/2013/12/national-security-agency-phones-judge-101203.html?hp=t1 |title=Judge: NSA phone program likely unconstitutional | publisher=Politico | author= Josh Gerstein | date=December 16, 2013 | access-date=2013-12-16}} Excerpts from his decision are as follows:{{Cite web |title=Klayman et al. v. Obama et al |url=https://ecf.dcd.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/show_public_doc?2013cv0851-48 |access-date=27 September 2024 |website=www.ecf.dcd.uscourts.gov}} {{blockquote|I cannot imagine a more "indiscriminate" and "arbitrary invasion" than this systematic and high-tech collection and retention of personal data on virtually every citizen [...] the almost-Orwellian technology [...] Records that once would have revealed a few scattered tiles of information about a person now reveal an entire mosaic – a vibrant constantly updating picture of a person's life. [[University of North Carolina School of Law|University of North Carolina]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) | footnotes = }} '''Richard Lesley Voorhees''' (born June 5, 1941) is a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Western District of North Carolina]]. ==Education and career== Voorhees was born in [[Syracuse, New York]]. He was in the [[United States Army]] as an ROTC cadet from 1959 to 1963. He received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[Davidson College]] in 1963 and a [[Juris Doctor]] from the [[University of North Carolina School of Law]] in 1968. He was in the [[United States Army Signal Corps]] as a Lieutenant from 1963 to 1965. He was an Army Reserves Captain from 1965 to 1969, and was in private practice in [[Gastonia, North Carolina]] from 1968 to 1988.{{FJC Bio|nid=1389211}} ===Federal judicial service=== On July 31, 1987, Voorhees was nominated by President [[Ronald Reagan]] to a seat on the [[United States District Court for the Western District of North Carolina]] vacated by Judge [[David B. Sentelle]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on October 14, 1988, and received his commission on October 17, 1988. He served as chief judge from 1991 to 1998. He assumed [[senior status]] on August 31, 2017. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Sources== * {{FJC Bio|nid=1389211}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[David B. Berman''' (born 1943) is a [[Senior status|senior]] [[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York]]. ==Education and early career== Berman received his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree from [[Cornell University]] in 1964. He earned his [[Juris Doctor]] from [[New York University School of Law]] in 1967. He received a Diploma of Comparative Law in 1968 and a Diploma of International Law in 1970 from the [[Stockholm University|University of Stockholm]] Faculty of Law, where he also served as Assistant to the Dean of Foreign Students. He received a [[Master of Social Work]] from [[Fordham Graduate School of Social Service]] in 1996. He went into private practice at [[Davis Polk & Wardwell]] in 1970. In 1974, he became Executive Assistant to [[United States Senator]] [[Jacob Javits]]. In 1977, he was named executive director of the New York State [[Alliance to Save Energy]], co-chaired by Senators Javits and [[Daniel Patrick Moynihan]]. A year later, he was appointed General Counsel and Executive Vice President of the [[Time Warner|Warner Cable Corporation]], a position he held until 1986, when he returned to private practice as a partner of LeBoeuf, Lamb, Greene & MacRae. ==Judicial career== Berman was appointed by Mayor Giuliani as judge of the [[New York State Family Court]] for [[Queens County, New York|Queens County]] (1995 to 1998).{{Cite web|title = Faculty Profile - Hon. Richard M. Berman|url = https://www.pli.edu/faculty/hon.-richard-m.-berman-i464347|website = pli.edu|access-date = 2024-06-18}} On May 21, 1998, he was named by President [[Bill Clinton]] to a seat on the District Court for the [[Southern District of New York]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on October 21, 1998. Berman assumed [[senior status]] on September 11, 2011. He is a member of the New York State-Federal Judicial Council, which is concerned with issues of interest to the state and federal judiciary. Berman served as Chairman of the council from 2011 to 2012. Berman is currently the Chairman of the Southern District of New York Senior Judges Committee. Berman was previously a co-chair of the Second Circuit Judicial Conference in 2005 and 2022. ==Notable cases== === U.S. District Court === ====''United States v. Ferguson''==== In June 2024, Berman presided over the criminal jury trial of Ricardo Ferguson for conspiracy to distribute crack cocaine, attempted Hobbs Act robbery, murder through the use of a firearm, and using and carrying a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking.{{Cite web|title = Bronx Man Convicted Of December 2021 Murder And Attempted Robbery In Aqueduct Park Walkway |url = https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/bronx-man-convicted-december-2021-murder-and-attempted-robbery-aqueduct-park-walkway| date=18 June 2024 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} Ferguson was found guilty on June 18, 2024.{{Cite web|title = Bronx Man Convicted Of December 2021 Murder And Attempted Robbery In Aqueduct Park Walkway |url = https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/bronx-man-convicted-december-2021-murder-and-attempted-robbery-aqueduct-park-walkway| date=18 June 2024 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} ====''United States v. Buyer''==== In March 2023, Berman presided over the criminal jury trial of former U.S. Congressman [[Stephen Buyer]] for “insider trading” for buying shares of Spring and Navigant Consulting before both were acquired by other companies, which he knew through his consulting work before the information was made public. He was found guilty on March 10, 2023. On September 19, 2023, Berman sentenced Buyer to a term of 22 months of incarceration and 3 years of supervised release. Buyer was also ordered to forfeit $354,027 in illegal gains and given a $10,000 fine.{{Cite web|title = Former congressman sentenced to nearly 2 years in prison for insider trading|url = https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/former-rep-stephen-buyer-sentenced-22-months-insider-trading-rcna105927|website = nbc.com| date=19 September 2023 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} ====''United States v. Hadden''==== In January 2023, Berman presided over the criminal jury trial of gynecologist [[Robert Hadden]] for sexually assaulting his patients during examinations. Berman sentenced Haden in July 2023 to the maximum term of 20 years of incarceration and a lifetime of supervised release.{{Cite web|title = Former Obstetrician/Gynecologist Robert Hadden Sentenced To 20 Years In Prison For Sexually Abusing Numerous Patients|url = https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/former-obstetriciangynecologist-robert-hadden-sentenced-20-years-prison-sexually|website = justice.gov| date=25 July 2023 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} ====''United States v. Halkbank''==== On October 15, 2019, Turkish bank [[Halkbank]] was indicted for allegedly conspiring to defraud the United States.{{Cite web|title = Turkish Bank Charged in Manhattan Federal Court for Its Participation in a Multibillion-Dollar Iranian Sanctions Evasion Scheme|url = https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/turkish-bank-charged-manhattan-federal-court-its-participation-multibillion-dollar-iranian|website = justice.gov| date=15 October 2019 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} In August 2020, Halkbank filed a motion to dismiss, alleging that the District Court lacked personal jurisdiction and that Halkbank is immune from liability under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act and “[[common law]]” principles. On October 1, 2020, Berman denied Halkbank's motion to dismiss, and on October 22, 2021, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed Berman's decision.{{Cite web|title = Turkey's Halkbank can be prosecuted over Iran sanction violations, U.S. appeals court rules |url =https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-appeals-court-says-turkeys-halkbank-can-be-prosecuted-over-iran-sanction-2021-10-22/|website = reuters.com| date=21 October 2021 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} The Supreme Court also rejected Halkbank's argument that it has immunity under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, but remanded to the Second Circuit to consider whether the bank has immunity under “common law” principles. In dissent, Justice Neil Gorsuch wrote that the Supreme Court's decision “overcomplicates the law for no good reason.” {{Cite web|title = US Supreme Court gives Turkey's Halkbank another chance to avoid charges |url =https://www.reuters.com/legal/us-supreme-court-gives-turkeys-halkbank-another-chance-avoid-charges-2023-04-19/|website = reuters.com| date=19 April 2023 |access-date = 2024-06-18}} ==== ''United States v. Atilla'' ==== In November and December 2017, Berman presided over the criminal jury trial of Turkish citizen [[Mehmet Hakan Atilla]]. Atilla was convicted of 5 out of 6 counts in the Indictment, including conspiracies to evade U.S. sanctions against Iran and to defraud the United States, and bank fraud. Atilla was sentenced on May 16, 2018, to 32 months in prison.{{Cite web|url=https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/turkish-banker-mehmet-hakan-atilla-sentenced-32-months-conspiring-violate-us-sanctions|title=Turkish Banker Mehmet Hakan Atilla Sentenced To 32 Months For Conspiring To Violate U.S. Sanctions Against Iran And Other Offenses|date=May 16, 2018|website=www.justice.gov}} ====''United States v. Owens et al''==== In September 2018, four individuals were charged in the “Panama Papers” conspiracy with unlawfully evading U.S. tax laws. Two of four defendants pleaded guilty to the charges. The remaining two defendants have not appeared in the S.D.N.Y. proceedings. ====''United States v. Epstein''==== In July 2019, Berman was assigned the case of financier [[Jeffrey Epstein]] who was charged with Sex Trafficking and Conspiracy to Commit Sex Trafficking. On July 18, 2019, Berman denied Epstein's bail application, finding that he posed a danger to the community and that he was also a flight risk. On July 23, 2019, Epstein attempted suicide at the Metropolitan Correctional Center (“MCC”) and on August 10, 2019, he committed suicide at the MCC. On August 27, 2019, Berman conducted a public hearing on the government's motion to dismiss the case. Twenty-seven alleged victims, along with the government and defense counsel, participated at the hearing.{{cite journal |last1=Cassell |first1=Paul |title=Hearing on Dismissing Epstein Charges Was Not 'Drama' but Proper Respect for Victims |journal=New York Law Journal |date=August 28, 2019 |url=https://www.law.com/newyorklawjournal/2019/08/28/hearing-on-dismissing-epstein-charges-was-not-drama-but-proper-respect-for-victims/?slreturn=20210123204300}} On August 29, 2019, Berman granted the motion to dismiss. ====''Ortiz v. United States''==== In March 2019, Berman denied an inmate's [[habeas corpus petition]] to vacate his six-year sentence. The Court held that the New York Penal Law § 120.05(7), or Second Degree Assault by a Convicted Prisoner, was a "crime of violence" under the [[United States Sentencing Guidelines]] and that Petitioner had waived his right to appeal.''Ortiz v. United States'', No. 13 CR. 687 (RMB), 2019 WL 1122869, at *1–6 (S.D.N.Y. Mar. 12, 2019) ====''Duka v. U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission''==== In August 2015, Berman enjoined the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] from continuing its securities law administrative proceedings against Barbara Duka, finding that the SEC's [[administrative law judge]]s had been appointed in violation of the [[Appointments Clause]] in the [[United States Constitution|U.S. Constitution]].{{Cite news|title = SEC Loses Second Round in Battle Over In-House Judges|url = https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-08-12/u-s-judge-blocks-sec-case-against-ex-s-p-executive-duka|website = Bloomberg.com|access-date = 2016-02-07|first = Bob Van Voris Patricia|last = Hurtado|date = 12 August 2015}}''Duka v. U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission'', No. 15 Civ. 357 (RMB) (SN) (S.D.N.Y. Aug. 12, 2015)[http://www.nysd.uscourts.gov/cases/show.php?db=special&id=482]{{Cite news|title = Federal Judge Rules SEC In-House Judges 'Likely Unconstitutional'|url = https://www.wsj.com/articles/federal-judge-rules-sec-in-house-judges-likely-unconstitutional-1439392986|newspaper = Wall Street Journal|access-date = 2016-02-11|issn = 0099-9660|first1 = Jean|last1 = Eaglesham|first2 = Timothy W.|last2 = Martin}} Upon appeal, the injunction was dissolved based upon the Second Circuit's holding in ''SEC v. Tilton'' that parties "must await a final SEC order before raising their Appointments Clause claim in federal court." On June 21, 2018, the Supreme Court of the United States in [[Lucia v. SEC]] resolved a "circuit split" and ruled that the SEC's ALJs are officers of the United States and, as Berman had also concluded, subject to the Appointments Clause. {{cite court |litigants=RAYMOND J.LUCIA ET AL. v. SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION |court=U.S. |opinion=No. 17–130 |reporter=U.S. |url=https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/17pdf/17-130_4f14.pdf |date=June 21, 2018 url-status=live}} ==== ''United States v. Rahimi'' ==== In October 2017, Berman presided over the criminal jury trial of [[Ahmad Khan Rahimi]], also known as the "Chelsea bomber." Rahimi was convicted of all counts related to the September 2016 bombing in the Chelsea neighborhood of New York City, in which 31 people were injured.{{cite news|last1=Wilson|first1=Michael|title=Chelsea Bomb Suspect Guilty in Attack That Sowed Terror Across Region|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/10/16/nyregion/chelsea-bombing-verdict.html|access-date=8 December 2017|work=The New York Times|date=16 October 2017}} Rahimi was sentenced on February 13, 2018, to life in prison. ====''NFL Management Council v. NFL Players Association ("Deflategate")''==== Berman presided over [[New England Patriots]] quarterback [[Tom Brady]]'s case involving a four-game suspension levied against him by the [[National Football League]] for Brady's alleged role in the 2015 "[[Deflategate]]" matter. After unsuccessful efforts to bring about a settlement, Berman overturned Brady's suspension in an opinion dated September 3, 2015, finding significant legal deficiencies attending Brady's suspension. These included the NFL's disregard of the rules and penalties regarding handling of footballs once they have left the locker room; denial of the opportunity for Brady to examine one of the two lead NFL investigators; and denial of access to investigative files.{{Cite court |opinion=15 Civ. 5916 |court=S.D.N.Y. |url=https://cbsboston.files.wordpress.com/2015/09/bermandecision.pdf |litigants=NATIONAL FOOTBALL LEAGUE MANAGEMENT COUNCIL, - v.- NATIONAL FOOTBALL LEAGUE PLAYERS ASSOCIATION |access-date=2015-09-03 |archive-date=2015-09-06 |date=September 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906070830/https://cbsboston.files.wordpress.com/2015/09/bermandecision.pdf |url-status=dead }} On April 25, 2016, a panel of the [[Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit]] reversed on the grounds that the ''Players Association'' had signed an arbitration agreement, and NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell's authority to implement the suspension. In dissent, Chief Judge [[Robert Katzmann]] determined that it was improper for the NFL Commissioner to review in arbitration his own decision to suspend Brady.''[https://www.ca2.uscourts.gov/decisions/isysquery/c5dbd602-1869-4ed5-bfa6-e1499082966b/1/doc/15-2801_complete_opn.pdf National Football League Management Council v. National Football League Players Ass'n]'' nos. 15‐2801, 15‐2805 (2d Cir. April 25, 2016) ====''United States v. Kurniawan''==== Berman has presided over two landmark wine cases. One involved [[Rudy Kurniawan]], who was convicted of counterfeiting fine wines in December 2013 following a jury trial, and sentenced to a term of incarceration.{{cite web|title=Accused Wine Counterfeiter Rudy Kurniawan Guilty in Landmark Case|url=https://www.winespectator.com/webfeature/show/id/49396|publisher=Wine Spectator|author=Peter Hellman|author2=Mitch Frank |access-date=20 December 2013}}{{cite web|url=https://www.fbi.gov/news/stories/2014/september/rare-wine-dealer-sentenced-in-counterfeiting-scheme|title=FBI — Rare Wine Dealer Sentenced in Counterfeiting Scheme|work=FBI}}{{cite news|last1=Gardiner|first1=Sean|last2=Sharp|first2=Sonja|title=Counterfeit Fine-Wine Dealer Sentenced to 10 Years|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/rudy-kurniawan-counterfeit-fine-wine-dealer-sentenced-to-10-years-in-prison-for-selling-fake-vintages-1407432096|publisher=The Wall Street Journal|date=August 7, 2014}} ====''Swedenburg v. Kelly''==== The second wine case involved a challenge to New York State liquor laws which prohibited out of state wineries from selling directly to consumers within New York. In November 2002, Berman held that New York's direct ban on such out of state wine sales was unconstitutional, as "[t]he New York regime constitutes a cut and dry example of direct discrimination against interstate commerce."''Swedenburg v. Kelly'', 232 F. Supp. 2d 135, 145 (S.D.N.Y. 2002), ''aff'd in part, rev'd in part and remanded'', 358 F.3d 223 (2d Cir. 2004), ''rev'd sub nom. Granholm v. Heald'', 544 U.S. 460 (2005)[https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=10392739179875629641&q=232+f+supp+2d+135&hl=en&as_sdt=2003] The ruling was upheld by the [[Supreme Court of the United States]] in [[Granholm v. Heald]].{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=13655407080576035263&q=544+U.S.+460&hl=en&as_sdt=2006|title=544 U.S. 460 (2005)}} ====''United States v. Siddiqui''==== Berman presided over the case against [[Aafia Siddiqui]], a Pakistani citizen and graduate of [[MIT]] and [[Brandeis University]], who was convicted by a jury in 2010 of attempted murder of U.S. officials in Afghanistan, and sentenced to lengthy incarceration.{{cite press release|url=https://www.justice.gov/usao/nys/pressreleases/February10/siddiquiaafiaverdictpr.pdf|title=Aafia Siddiqui Found Guilty in Manhattan Federal Court of Attempting to Murder U.S. Nationals in Afghanistan and Six Additional Charges|publisher=Public Information Office, United States Attorney Southern District of New York|date=3 February 2010|access-date=13 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216055927/http://www.justice.gov/usao/nys/pressreleases/February10/siddiquiaafiaverdictpr.pdf|archive-date=16 February 2010|url-status=dead}} {{PD-notice}}{{Cite news|title = Aafia Siddiqui Guilty of Shooting at Americans in Afghanistan|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2010/02/04/nyregion/04siddiqui.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 2010-02-03|access-date = 2016-02-07|issn = 0362-4331|first = C. J.|last = Hughes}} ====''New York Taxi Workers Alliance v. New York City Taxi & Limousine Commission''==== In September 2007, Berman denied the NYC cab driver association's application to prevent the [[New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission]] from requiring that all taxicabs must be installed with credit- and debit-card readers.{{cite web|url=http://cityroom.blogs.nytimes.com/2007/09/28/federal-judge-refuses-to-block-credit-cards-video-screens-and-gps-in-taxis/?_r=0|title=Federal Judge Refuses to Block Credit Cards, Video Screens and G.P.S. in Taxis|first=Sewell|last=Chan|date=28 September 2007}} ====''MacWade v. Kelly''==== In December 2005, following a bench trial, Berman ruled that random police searches of riders' backpacks and bags on the New York City subway system do not violate the U.S. Constitution.''MacWade v. Kelly'', No. 05 Civ. 6921 (RMB), 2005 WL 3338573, at *1 (S.D.N.Y. Dec. 7, 2005), ''aff'd'', 460 F.3d 260 (2d Cir. 2006).[https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=15868425164922115182&q=460+f3d+260&hl=en&as_sdt=2003] ==== ''Gershkovich v. Iocco'' ==== Alex Gershkovich, a photographer involved in the Occupy Wall Street movement, sued two NYPD officers and the City of New York claiming that he was arrested without probable cause while photographing police activity in a public place. Berman, in a summary judgment decision dated July 17, 2017, determined that the right to record police activity in public areas was "clearly established" at the time of Gerskovich's arrest. The parties reached a settlement in November 2017.''Gerskovich v. Iocco'', No. 15 CIV. 7280 (RMB), 2017 WL 3236445 (S.D.N.Y. July 17, 2017) ==== ''Gordon v. Softech International, Inc.'' ==== After having determined that the [[Driver's Privacy Protection Act|Driver's Privacy Protection Act of 1994]] ("DPPA") is not a "strict liability" statute, Berman presided over the civil jury trial against defendants Arcanum Investigations, Inc. and its executive director. On April 24, 2015, the jury found that defendants, who are resellers of [[Department of Motor Vehicles|DMV]] information were not liable. They had used reasonable care in providing plaintiff's information to a third party. By summary order, dated April 15, 2016, the Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed the judgment entered in connection with the jury's verdict.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ca2.uscourts.gov/decisions/isysquery/daacde16-cc0c-4cae-b98f-ce57070e9a06/24/doc/15-1635_so.pdf#xml=http://www.ca2.uscourts.gov/decisions/isysquery/daacde16-cc0c-4cae-b98f-ce57070e9a06/24/hilite/|title=Summary Order|date=April 15, 2016|website=U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit}} ====''United States v. D'Souza''==== Berman presided in the [[Dinesh D'Souza]] campaign finance case in May 2014. On the eve of trial, D'Souza pleaded guilty to campaign finance violations, (arranging straw donors), and was sentenced in September 2014 to five years of probation, $30,000 fine, and community service.{{Cite news|title = D'Souza Avoids Prison in Campaign Finance Case|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2014/09/24/us/dsouza-is-spared-prison-time-for-campaign-finance-violations.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 2014-09-23|access-date = 2016-02-10|issn = 0362-4331|first = Jonathan|last = Mahler}} ====''Ideal Steel Supply Corporation v. Anza''==== In June 2002, Berman dismissed a civil RICO suit against National Steel Supply, Inc., finding that plaintiff Ideal Steel failed to show that it had relied upon National Steel Supply's alleged misrepresentations to the [[New York State Department of Taxation and Finance]]. The decision was [[Anza v. Ideal Steel Supply Corp.|affirmed]] by the U.S. Supreme Court on June 5, 2006.{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=9875457426421386488&q=547+U.S.+451&hl=en&as_sdt=2003|title=''Anza v. Ideal Steel Supply Corp.'', 547 U.S. 451 (2006)}} ==== ''United States v. Leekin'' ==== In July 2008, Berman presided over the criminal case against Judith Leekin, who pleaded guilty to defrauding New York City and New York State adoption agencies out of $1.68 million in foster care funds. Leekin also had mistreated and willfully endangered her (11) adopted special needs children.{{Cite news|title = One Woman, 11 Adoptions and a Time of Urgency|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/02/nyregion/02adopt.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 2007-08-02|access-date = 2016-02-07|issn = 0362-4331|first = Leslie|last = Kaufman}} Berman sentenced Leekin to 130 months in prison. She was also prosecuted for child abuse in Florida.{{Cite web|title = Fla. woman in adoption scam gets 20 years|url = https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna29035972|website = msnbc.com| date=5 February 2009 |access-date = 2016-02-07}} ==== ''Dimmie v. Carey'' ==== In April 2000, Berman dismissed the infringement suit brought against pop singer [[Mariah Carey]], finding that the plaintiff, Rhonda Dimmie, the holder of a [[copyright]] for the song ''Be Your Hero'', had failed to show that Carey, the copyright-holder for the song ''[[Hero (Mariah Carey song)|Hero]]'', had knowledge of or infringed upon plaintiff's recording.''Dimmie v. Carey'', 88 F. Supp. 2d 142 (S.D.N.Y. 2000) {{Cite web|title = Pop singer cleared of copyright infringement|url = http://www.recordonline.com/article/20000224/news/302249998|website = recordonline.com|access-date = 2016-02-07|first=Beth|last=Kalet|publisher=The Times Herald-Record}} ==== ''Johnson v. Johnson'' ==== In January 2011, Berman presided over a trial in which a father sought the return of his child from New York to [[Vicenza|Vicenza, Italy]] pursuant to the [[Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction|Hague Convention]] of the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. Following a bench trial, Berman found that Italy was not the habitual residence of the child, who also strenuously objected to being returned to Italy.''Johnson v. Johnson'', No. 11 Civ. 37 (RMB), 2011 WL 569876 (S.D.N.Y. Feb. 10, 2011) === Family Court Case === ==== ''In the Matter of Shawna E.'' ==== In January 1998, as a New York State family court judge, Berman removed two children from the custody of then professional baseball player [[Carl Everett]] and his wife. The Everetts had consented to findings of child neglect following the discovery of bruises on their daughter at the [[Shea Stadium]] child care center.{{Cite journal|title = Matter of Everett|date = April 23, 1998|journal = New York Law Journal |at= 30, col. 5 [Fam. Ct. Queens Cnty. 1998]}}{{Cite news|title = Everett Fails to Get Custody|url = https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/09/sports/everett-fails-to-get-custody.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 1997-08-09|access-date = 2016-02-11|issn = 0362-4331}}{{Cite news|title = D.A. Still Looking Into Everett Abuse Case|url = https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/10/sports/da-still-looking-into-everett-abuse-case.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 1997-08-10|access-date = 2016-02-11|issn = 0362-4331|first = Mirta|last = Ojito}} === U.S. District Court 3 Judge Panels === ==== ''Rodriguez v. Pataki'' ==== Berman was part of a three-judge panel that heard challenges to the redistricting plan enacted by the New York State Legislature following the [[2000 United States census|2000 census]]. Following a bench trial in November 2003, the three-judge panel found that New York's redistricting plan did not violate the [[Voting Rights Act of 1965|Voting Rights Act]] or the [[Equal Protection Clause]] of the [[Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Fourteenth Amendment]].{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=17491384514542603163&q=308+f+supp+2d+346&hl=en&as_sdt=2003|title=''Rodriguez v. Pataki'', 308 F. Supp. 2d 346 (S.D.N.Y. 2004)}} In November 2004, the U.S. Supreme Court affirmed by summary order.{{cite web|url=https://law.resource.org/pub/us/case/reporter/US/543/543.US.997.04-218.html|title=543 U.S. 997|website=law.resource.org}} ==== ''[[Nitke v. Gonzales]]'' ==== Berman was part of a three-judge panel that heard challenges to obscenity provisions of the [[Communications Decency Act]] of 1996. In July 2005, the Court found that the Act was not overbroad and did not violate the [[First Amendment to the United States Constitution|First Amendment]].{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=12057951921706678117&q=413+f+supp+2d+262&hl=en&as_sdt=2003|title=''Nitke v. Gonzales'', 413 F. Supp. 2d 262 (S.D.N.Y. 2005)}} In March 2006, the U.S. Supreme Court affirmed by summary order.{{Cite journal|title = Nitke v. Gonzales|date = January 2006|journal = Berkeley Technology Law Journal |volume=21 |issue=1}} === U.S. Circuit Court Opinions === ==== ''Carpenters Pension Trust Fund of St. Louis v. Barclays PLC'' ==== In April 2014, Berman—sitting by designation on the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit|U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit]]—authored the panel's opinion reinstating a securities fraud class action brought by pension funds against [[Barclays|Barclays PLC]] and former Barclays' CEO [[Bob Diamond (banker)|Robert Diamond]]. Plaintiffs alleged that defendants had knowingly submitted false and inaccurate information to establish [[Libor|LIBOR]] rates during the class period of August 2007 through January 2009. The Court adopted the principle that "so long as the falsehood remains uncorrected, it will continue to taint the total mix of available public information, and the market will continue to attribute the artificial inflation to the stock, day after day."''Carpenters Pension Trust Fund of St. Louis v. Barclays PLC'', 750 F.3d 227 (2d Cir. 2014)[https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=18296911101080105261&q=750+F.3d+227&hl=en&as_sdt=2003]''See also In re Harman International Industries, Inc. Securities Litigation'', 791 F.3d 90 (D.C. Cir. 2015)[https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=18379824855121259506&q=791+F.3d+90&hl=en&as_sdt=2003] ==== ''Evans v. Books-A-Million'' ==== In August 2014, Berman—sitting by designation on a panel of the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit|U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit]]—heard the appeal of an employee who had been terminated from her job. The Court of Appeals held that the district court correctly awarded summary judgment to plaintiff on her COBRA claims and to Books-A-Million with respect to plaintiff's Title VII and Equal Pay Act claims, but erred in dismissing plaintiff's FMLA claims. The Court of Appeals found that "[i]if a trial court refuses to grant further legal or equitable relief to a plaintiff who insists that such relief is necessary to make the plaintiff whole, it must articulate its rationale."{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=7924063185439270003&q=762+f3d+1288&hl=en&as_sdt=2003|title=''Evans v. Books-A-Million'', 762 F.3d 1288, 1296 (11th Cir. 2014)}} ==== ''New England Insurance Co. v. Healthcare Underwriters Mutual Insurance Co.'' ==== In July 2002, Berman—sitting by designation on a panel of the Second Circuit Court of Appeals—heard the appeal of New England Insurance Company, following the district court's reversal of a jury verdict in favor of New England Insurance. The Second Circuit reinstated the jury verdict. "We necessarily disagree with the 'clear liability' language []introduced by the district court in deciding Healthcare's post-trial application for judgment as a matter of law. As noted, 'clear liability' was specifically rejected and abandoned [and] there is no case since ''Pavia'' in which a court held that a finding of clear liability was given conclusive or totally dispositive weight."''New England Insurance Co. v. Healthcare Underwriters Mutual Insurance Co.'', 295 F.3d 232, 242-43 (2d Cir. 2002)[https://scholar.google.com/scholar_case?case=4778551811127404915&q=295+f3d+232&hl=en&as_sdt=2003] == Publications and Teaching == Berman has authored a number of articles about children, including ''A Team Model To Identify Child Abuse'',{{Cite journal |last=Berman |first=Richard M. |date=January 26, 2006 |title=A Team Model To Identify Child Abuse |journal=New York Law Journal}} ''Seven Steps To Protect Children'',{{Cite journal |last=Berman |first=Richard M. |date=February 28, 2006 |title=Seven Steps To Protect Children |journal=New York Law Journal}} ''Community Service for Juvenile Offenders'',{{Cite journal |last=Berman |first=Richard M. |date=March 15, 2010 |title=Community Service for Juvenile Offenders |journal=New York Law Journal}} and ''Special Immigrant Juvenile Status''.{{Cite journal |last=Berman |first=Richard M. |date=March 3, 2015 |title=Special Immigrant Juvenile Status |journal=New York Law Journal}}{{Cite news |last=Russo |first=Melissa |date=June 1, 2015 |title=I-Team: Federal Probe Finds "Reasonable Suspicion" of Criminal Activity in Alleged Scheme to Defraud Queens Family Court |url=http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Immigration-Fraud-Queens-Family-Court-I-Team-Russo-Investigation-New-York-Government-SIngh-Green-Card-305701981.html |access-date=February 7, 2016}} Published in the [[New York Law Journal]], these articles offer guidance in developing improved models for identifying child abuse, bolstering the child welfare system, implementing community service-based sentencing options for juvenile offenders, and improving the process for obtaining special immigrant juvenile status. Berman's efforts in improving media access to the Family Court system and promoting community service have been cited in the [[Daily News (New York)|New York Daily News]] and [[Newsday]]. ''See, e.g.'', ''Sun Also Rises in Family Court'',{{Cite web |title=SUN ALSO RISES IN FAMILY COURT |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/opinions/sun-rises-family-court-article-1.779658 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220090208/http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/opinions/sun-rises-family-court-article-1.779658 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 20, 2016 |access-date=2016-02-11 |website=NY Daily News|date=15 August 1997 }} ''Helping Other Helps Teens'',{{Cite news |last=Serant |first=Claire |date=October 20, 1996 |title=Helping Others Helps Teens Troubled Kids Learn Kindness |work=Daily News |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/boroughs/helping-helps-teens-troubled-kids-learn-kindness-article-1.744767 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220085909/http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/boroughs/helping-helps-teens-troubled-kids-learn-kindness-article-1.744767 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 20, 2016 |access-date=February 7, 2016}} ''Embracing Community Service for Juveniles'',{{Cite news |last=English |first=Merle |date=August 31, 1997 |title=Embracing Community Service for Juveniles |work=Newsday}} and ''A New Way Out of Trouble''.{{Cite news |last=Bertrand |first=Donald |date=December 24, 1997 |title=A New Way Out of Trouble: Young Offenders Get Alternatives to Jail |work=Daily News}} Berman lectured about the "Rule of Law" before judges in [[Albania]] in 2013. He has also moderated a panel discussion of the "Rule of Law" at an international legal symposium in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]] in 2014.{{Cite web |title=Rule of law and freedom of press under attack in Turkey |url=https://www.cihan.com.tr/en/rule-of-law-and-freedom-of-press-under-attack-in-turkey-1428007.htm? |access-date=2016-03-24 |website=Cihan Haber Ajansı: Doğru ve hızlı haberin adresi}} == Federal Court Involvement in Supervised Release == Berman has been actively involved in the supervised release of all defendants (201) whom he sentenced to incarceration.{{Cite web|last=Berman|first=Richard|date=2022-10-12|title=Court Involvement in Supervised Release |url=https://sentencing.typepad.com/files/judge-berman-supervised-release-report-2022.10.12.pdf|access-date=2024-06-18|language=en-US}} Between January 1, 2020, and June 18, 2024, Berman has conducted over 960 supervised release hearings.{{Cite web|website=Fordham Urban Law Journal | date=2024|title=Beyond Bars: Rethinking Substance Use Criminalization in Federal Supervised Release |url=https://ir.lawnet.fordham.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2974&context=ulj|access-date=2024-06-18|language=en-US}} Drawing upon his MSW studies and Family Court experience, this Court Involved Supervised Release project has produced positive supervised release outcomes (regarding recidivism/desistance and successful termination of supervision) which are detailed in five written reports, dated April 2021, September 2021, April 2022, October 2022, and June 2024.{{Cite web|last=Review|first=The Regulatory|date=2021-06-28|title=Federal Court Involvement in Supervised Release {{!}} The Regulatory Review|url=https://www.theregreview.org/2021/06/28/berman-federal-court-involvement-supervised-release/|access-date=2021-07-03|website=www.theregreview.org|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|url=http://pli.edu/Content/Faculty/Hon_Richard_M_Berman/_/N-4oZ1z13eyo?ID=PE464347|title=Faculty Profile - Hon. Richard M. Berman|website=pli.edu|access-date=2016-05-06}} On October 13, 2021, Berman participated on a panel with the Honorable L. Felipe Restrepo for the Penn Program on Regulation titled How Judges Can Make a Difference in the Success of Supervised Release.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3wUWHAJKpz4 |title=How Judges Can Make a Difference in the Success of Supervised Release (October 13, 2021) |website=[[YouTube]] |date=15 October 2021 }} ==Awards== Berman received the [[National Association of Social Workers]] (NYC) Emerald award for 20 years of leadership as a licensed social worker and judge on March 28, 2019.{{Cite web|url=https://www.naswnyc.org/page/236|title=Leadership Awards Dinner - National Association of Social Workers New York City|website=www.naswnyc.org}} == See also == * [[List of Jewish American jurists]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FJC Bio|nid=1390791}} {{s-start}} {{s-legal}} {{s-bef|before=[[Kevin Thomas Duffy]]}} {{s-ttl|title={{nowrap|Judge of the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York]]}}|years=1998–2011}} {{s-aft|after=[[Nelson S. [[Columbia University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''Richard Gus Seeborg'''{{cite web|url=https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/RichardSeeborg-PublicQuestionnaire.pdf|title=Questionnaire for Judicial Nominees|work=United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|date=September 23, 2009}} (born November 4, 1956) is an American lawyer and jurist serving as a [[United States federal judge|U.S. district judge]] of the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of California]]. He was appointed in 2010 by President [[Barack Obama]], and he served as chief judge of the court from 2021 to 2026. Seeborg was a [[United States magistrate judge]] in the same district prior to his appointment. == Early life and education == Seeborg was born in 1956 in [[Landstuhl]] town, [[Kaiserslautern]] district, [[Rhineland-Palatinate]] state, Germany.{{Cite web |title=Chief District Judge Richard Seeborg |url=https://www.cand.uscourts.gov/judges/seeborg-richard-rs/ |website=United States District Court Northern District of California |access-date=September 13, 2024 |archive-date=September 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907070557/https://cand.uscourts.gov/judges/seeborg-richard-rs/ |url-status=live }} Seeborg received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] ''[[summa cum laude]]'' with a major in history from [[Yale University]] in May 1978 and a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[Columbia Law School]] in 1981.{{cite web|url=http://www.legalspan.com/catalog2/faculty.asp?UserID=20011211147985115059++++++&OwnerColor=#A55A9C|title=Hon. Richard G. Seeborg|website=www.legalspan.com|access-date=May 24, 2017|archive-date=October 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181026222656/http://www.legalspan.com/catalog2/faculty.asp?UserID=20011211147985115059++++++&OwnerColor=#A55A9C|url-status=live}} From 1981 to 1982, Seeborg served as a [[law clerk]] to Judge [[John H. Pratt]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]].{{FJC Bio|nid=1392981|inline=yes}} == Career == In 1982, Seeborg joined the [[San Francisco]] law firm of [[Morrison & Foerster]] as an associate. He became a partner with the firm in 1987. In 1991, Seeborg left Morrison & Foerster to become an [[assistant United States attorney]] for the Northern District of California in [[San Jose, California]]. He served in that post until 1998, when he returned to Morrison & Foerster, working as a partner and focusing on a litigation practice in the fields of [[securities]], [[intellectual property]], and general [[commercial law|commercial matters]]. === Federal judicial service === On February 9, 2001, Seeborg became a United States magistrate judge for the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of California]]. On August 7, 2009, President [[Barack Obama]] nominated Seeborg to be a United States district judge on the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of California]].[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the_press_office/President-Obama-Nominates-Edward-Milton-Chen-Dolly-Gee-and-Richard-Seeborg-to-Serve-on-the-District-Court-Bench President Obama Nominates Edward Milton Chen, Dolly Gee and Richard Seeborg to Serve on the District Court Bench] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090901061740/http://www.whitehouse.gov/the_press_office/President-Obama-Nominates-Edward-Milton-Chen-Dolly-Gee-and-Richard-Seeborg-to-Serve-on-the-District-Court-Bench/ |date=September 1, 2009 }}, ''[[whitehouse.gov]]'' (August 7, 2009). On October 15, 2009, the [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary]] voted to send Seeborg's nomination to the full Senate.{{cite news |first=Howard |last=Mintz |title=Senate Judiciary Committee votes to confirm two Bay Area federal judge nominees |work=Contra Costa Times |date=October 17, 2009 }} The Senate confirmed Seeborg by unanimous consent on December 24, 2009. He received his commission on January 4, 2010. He became chief judge on February 1, 2021, after [[Phyllis J. Hamilton]] assumed [[senior status]].{{Cite press release |title=Chief District Judge Phyllis J. Hamilton Assumes Senior Status |url=https://www.cand.uscourts.gov/notices/chief-district-judge-phyllis-j-hamilton-assumes-senior-status/ |access-date=February 1, 2021 |archive-date=January 28, 2021
